**Adrián González Savín** (born May 8, 1982), also known by his nicknames "**A-Gon**" and "**Titán**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-1) is a Mexican-American former professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball")[first baseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_baseman "First baseman"). He played in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB) for the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"), [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres"), [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox"), [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), and [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").

González was born in the United States, but was raised in [Tijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana "Tijuana"), Baja California, Mexico, until 1990, when he returned to the United States. He played for [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team") in the [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Baseball_Classic "2006 World Baseball Classic"), [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Baseball_Classic "2009 World Baseball Classic"), [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Baseball_Classic "2013 World Baseball Classic"), and the [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic "2017 World Baseball Classic") editions of the [World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Baseball_Classic "World Baseball Classic") and the [2020 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Baseball at the 2020 Summer Olympics").

González was the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_Major_League_Baseball_draft_picks "List of first overall Major League Baseball draft picks") in the [2000 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2000 Major League Baseball draft") by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins"). He was traded to the Rangers, and made his MLB debut with them in 2004. He was traded to the Padres after the 2005 season, where he was an [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "Major League Baseball All-Star Game") selection three times and a two-time [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawlings_Gold_Glove_Award "Rawlings Gold Glove Award") winner. He was traded to the Red Sox after the 2010 season, and was traded to the Dodgers in August 2012. After playing for the Dodgers throughout the 2017 season, he was traded to the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves"), but was released without playing for them. He then played for the Mets, who released him during the 2018 season.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Adrián González was born in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California, to David and Alba González, both Mexican natives.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-3) González is the youngest of three boys; his brothers are David Jr. and [Edgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)"), a former big leaguer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-little-4) After his birth, his parents moved the family to [Tijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana "Tijuana"), where his father owned an air-conditioner business.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2) The three boys grew up playing baseball in Mexico,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2) where their father had been a member of the [Mexico national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5) In 1990, the family returned to the United States, settling in [Bonita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonita,_California "Bonita, California").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5)

While Adrián was drafted by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins") out of high school, his brother [Edgar Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)") attended [San Diego State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_State_University "San Diego State University") and was selected by the [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays") in the 30th round of the 2000 draft.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5) Edgar debuted in the major leagues as a utility man with the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") in 2008, joining his brother as a teammate.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-6)

In 2012, David and Alba González were named George and Barbara Bush Little League Parents of the Year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-little-4) In November 2012, González was honored as one of 30 "exemplary citizens" by the mayor of Tijuana in an official ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)

González was projected to be a late first-round pick out of [Eastlake High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastlake_High_School_(Chula_Vista,_California) "Eastlake High School (Chula Vista, California)") in [Chula Vista, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chula_Vista,_California "Chula Vista, California");[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-8) however, his stock increased with his senior-year performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-9) In his senior year, he hit .645 with 13 home runs and 34 runs batted in.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-10)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Florida Marlins (2000–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Florida Marlins (2000–2003)")]

In June 2000, González became the first infield position player to be drafted first overall since [Alex Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Rodriguez "Alex Rodriguez") in 1993. He was given a $3 million signing bonus by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-11) While in the Marlins organization, González played with the [Gulf Coast League Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_League_Marlins "Gulf Coast League Marlins"), [Kane County Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kane_County_Cougars "Kane County Cougars"), [Utica Blue Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica_Blue_Sox "Utica Blue Sox"), [Portland Sea Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Sea_Dogs "Portland Sea Dogs") (2002),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-12)[Albuquerque Isotopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Isotopes "Albuquerque Isotopes") (2003), and [Carolina Mudcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Mudcats_(1991%E2%80%932011) "Carolina Mudcats (1991–2011)") (2003). With the Single-A Kane County Cougars in his second professional season, González hit .312 with 17 home runs and 103 RBIs in 127 games. As a result, he was selected by the [Midwest League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League "Midwest League") as its [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Midwest League Most Valuable Player Award") and [Prospect of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League_Prospect_of_the_Year_Award "Midwest League Prospect of the Year Award"). He also played in the [All-Star Futures Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Futures_Game "All-Star Futures Game").

### Texas Rangers (2004–2005)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Texas Rangers (2004–2005)")]

After a wrist injury, the Marlins felt González would be hindered swinging the bat, so they included González in a June 2003 trade with the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"), along with [Ryan Snare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Snare "Ryan Snare") and minor leaguer Will Smith, to acquire relief pitcher [Ugueth Urbina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugueth_Urbina "Ugueth Urbina") to aid their championship drive.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-13) González played with the Rangers' Class-AA team, the [Frisco RoughRiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisco_RoughRiders "Frisco RoughRiders"), until he made his major-league debut against the [Seattle Mariners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Mariners "Seattle Mariners") on April 18, 2004. He was hitless in three at-bats. He recorded his first base hit on April 20 against [Ramón Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Ortiz "Ramón Ortiz") of the [Anaheim Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Angels "Anaheim Angels") and his first home run on April 25 off [Kevin Jarvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Jarvis "Kevin Jarvis") of the Seattle Mariners. He played in 16 games for Texas in 2004 and in 43 games in 2005, with a combined batting average of .229 and 7 homers.

### San Diego Padres (2006–2010)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: San Diego Padres (2006–2010)")]

#### 2006

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2006")]

After the season, González was traded to the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") along with pitcher [Chris Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Young_(pitcher) "Chris Young (pitcher)") and [outfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outfielder "Outfielder")[Terrmel Sledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrmel_Sledge "Terrmel Sledge"). In return, the Rangers received [Adam Eaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Eaton_(pitcher) "Adam Eaton (pitcher)") and [Akinori Otsuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akinori_Otsuka "Akinori Otsuka"). Originally seen as an eventual replacement for [Ryan Klesko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Klesko "Ryan Klesko") at first base, González was given the job when Klesko underwent shoulder surgery.

With extended playing time at first base in 2006, González continued to improve his hitting and defense. On July 23, 2006, he was named the [NL Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NL_Player_of_the_Week "NL Player of the Week").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-14) In his first full season, he led the Padres in [batting average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") (.304) and [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") (24). He was the first player in [Petco Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petco_Park "Petco Park") history to have more than one multiple home run game. He was named the Padres MVP for 2006.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2007

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2007")]

On March 31, 2007, González agreed to a $9.5 million, four-year deal, with a club option for $5.5 million in 2011.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-16) In the 2007 season, he led the Padres in home runs again, with 30, and had a team-high 100 RBIs. He led all Major League first basemen with 161 games and a career-high 46 doubles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2008

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2008")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg/330px-Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg)

González after a swing with the [Padres in 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_San_Diego_Padres_season "2008 San Diego Padres season")

In the 2008 season, González finished with a .279 average and once again led the Padres with 36 home runs and 119 RBIs. He was elected to the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2008 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") as a reserve. In the exhibition, he went 1 for 3 with a single and a sacrifice fly, driving in [Miguel Tejada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Tejada "Miguel Tejada"). He won his first [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Glove_Award "Gold Glove Award") in 2008 at first base and set career highs in games played (162), home runs (36), RBI (119), runs scored (103), walks (74), and slugging percentage (.510). He was named the Padres MVP for the second time.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2009

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2009")]

González played winter ball in the [Mexican Pacific League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Pacific_League "Mexican Pacific League") with the [Venados de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venados_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Venados de Mazatlán"). In the [Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Caribbean_Series "2009 Caribbean Series"), he led his team past the Dominican Republic's [Tigres del Licey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigres_del_Licey "Tigres del Licey") with a record-setting 3 home runs on February 4.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-17)

González hit 23 homers, leading the majors in that category through May 2009 despite playing his home games at Petco Park, which Padres statisticians describe as an "extreme [pitcher's park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitcher's_park "Pitcher's park")."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb.mlb.com-18) On May 18, González was described as being one of the two most underrated players in the National League according to an [MLB.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB.com "MLB.com") poll of major league executives and managers.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb.mlb.com-18) On June 1, he was named the NL Co-[Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") for the second time in his career. During that week, González hit four home runs, tallied 10 RBIs, and had a 1.000 slugging percentage.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-19) González was elected to the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2009 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") after voting by fellow players, managers and coaches.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-20) He subsequently participated in that year's [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby "Home Run Derby"), where he hit two home runs in the first round. On August 1, González batted 6-for-6 with three [RBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in") as the Padres topped the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") 13–6. González's six hits are the most by any Padre in a nine-inning game. Three others have accomplished the feat, but did it in extra-inning contests. González hit five singles and a double.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-21)

He led the majors in walks in 2009 with 119[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-22) and set a major league record with eight consecutive multi-walk games,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-23) a record which still stands as of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-24) He also hit 40 home runs for the first time in his career. He was named the Padres team MVP for 2009, his third time honored.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2010")]

González started the 2010 season playing well. On May 24, he was named the NL Player of the Week for the fourth time in his career.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-25) On June 2, González hit a [walk-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk-off_home_run "Walk-off home run")[grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_(baseball) "Grand slam (baseball)") in the eleventh inning of a 5–1 victory over the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-26) In July, González was elected to participate in his third consecutive [All-Star game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2010 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").

During the 2010 season, González had 176 hits in 591 at-bats, good for a .298 batting average, his highest since hitting .304 in 2006. His 93 walks put him in third place in the NL behind only [Prince Fielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Fielder "Prince Fielder") (114) and [Albert Pujols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Pujols "Albert Pujols") (103). He finished with 31 home runs and 101 RBI, the third time in his career he had 100 RBI or more. González played in 160 games on the year, tying him with [Rickie Weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickie_Weeks "Rickie Weeks") for 5th in the NL. He scored 87 runs on the season, compiling 302 [total bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_base "Total base"), which also tied him with Weeks, for 6th in the NL. González was named team MVP for the third consecutive year and the fourth time overall with the Padres.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-27)

### Boston Red Sox (2011–2012)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Boston Red Sox (2011–2012)")]

On December 6, 2010, González was traded to the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox") for a package of right-handed pitcher [Casey Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Kelly "Casey Kelly"), first baseman [Anthony Rizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Rizzo "Anthony Rizzo"), outfielder [Reymond Fuentes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reymond_Fuentes "Reymond Fuentes"), and a [player to be named later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_to_be_named_later "Player to be named later"), later determined to be [Eric Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Patterson_(baseball) "Eric Patterson (baseball)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-29)

On April 15, 2011, González and the Red Sox agreed to a seven-year contract extension worth $154 million through the 2018 season.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-30) On June 19, González hit his 1,000th career hit: a triple off of [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") pitcher [Yovani Gallardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yovani_Gallardo "Yovani Gallardo").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-l452-31)

On July 3, 2011, González was selected to the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2011 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") in Arizona along with teammates [Josh Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Beckett "Josh Beckett"), [Jacoby Ellsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacoby_Ellsbury "Jacoby Ellsbury"), [David Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ortiz "David Ortiz"), [Kevin Youkilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Youkilis "Kevin Youkilis"), and [Jon Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Lester "Jon Lester"). González hit a home run in the game and was responsible for the only run for the [American League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_League "American League"). Additionally, Ortiz selected González as one of three sluggers to join him in the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby "Home Run Derby"), where he finished second to [Robinson Canó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robinson_Can%C3%B3 "Robinson Canó"). González tied a record for most home runs in the final round of the home run derby at 11, which was then surpassed by the victor Canó.

González was named AL [Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for June 2011 with a .404 average (40 for 99) – the best in the Majors for that month.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-32) After placing second in the [2011 Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Major_League_Baseball_Home_Run_Derby "2011 Major League Baseball Home Run Derby"), González faced a home-run slump until he hit five home runs in ten at-bats on August 23–25.

On November 21, González finished seventh in MVP voting, trailing his teammate Ellsbury in second and the winner, [Detroit Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Tigers "Detroit Tigers") ace [Justin Verlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Verlander "Justin Verlander").

González appeared on the cover of baseball video game _[MLB 12: The Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB\_12:\_The\_Show "MLB 12: The Show")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-33) In 2012, González appeared in 123 games with the Red Sox, hitting .300 with 15 homers and 86 RBI.

### Los Angeles Dodgers (2012–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Los Angeles Dodgers (2012–2017)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21%2C_2013.jpg/250px-Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21%2C_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21,_2013.jpg)

González in 2013

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2012")]

On August 25, 2012, González was traded to the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers") (along with [Josh Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Beckett "Josh Beckett"), [Nick Punto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Punto "Nick Punto") and [Carl Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Crawford "Carl Crawford")) and $11 million in cash for [James Loney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Loney "James Loney"), [Iván DeJesús Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iv%C3%A1n_DeJes%C3%BAs_Jr. "Iván DeJesús Jr."), [Allen Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Webster_(baseball) "Allen Webster (baseball)") and two players to be named later ([Jerry Sands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Sands "Jerry Sands") and [Rubby De La Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubby_De_La_Rosa "Rubby De La Rosa")).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-34) In his first at bat with the Dodgers that same day, he hit a three-run home run against the [Miami Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Marlins "Miami Marlins").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-35) In 36 games with the Dodgers, he hit .297 with 3 homers and 22 RBI.

#### 2013

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2013")]

In the 2013 season, González appeared in 157 games for the Dodgers and hit .293 with 22 home runs and 100 RBI. He was a candidate for the [final vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Final_Vote "All-Star Final Vote") at the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2013 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") but was not chosen for the game.

In Game 5 of the [NLCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_National_League_Championship_Series "2013 National League Championship Series") against the [St. Louis Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals"), González went 3 for 4 with 2 home runs. The Dodgers would eventually lose the series in six games.

#### 2014

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2014")]

González finished the 2014 season with 116 RBI, most in the majors. He was the Dodgers' nominee for the [Hank Aaron Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Aaron_Award "Hank Aaron Award"), after hitting 27 home runs in 159 games. However, his batting average of .276 was the lowest of his career. He finished up the season by winning the [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award") for NL first baseman and also won several awards for his defense at first base, including the [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Glove_Award "Gold Glove Award"), [Fielding Bible Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_Bible_Award "Fielding Bible Award") and [Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Sporting_Goods "Wilson Sporting Goods").

#### 2015

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: 2015")]

González opened the 2015 season with five home runs in the first three games of the season, including three on April 8 against [Andrew Cashner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cashner "Andrew Cashner"). He was the first MLB player to hit five home runs in the first three games of the season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-36) By homering in his fifth consecutive game, dating back to the end of the 2014 season, he tied the team record, which he shares with [Roy Campanella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Campanella "Roy Campanella") (1950), [Shawn Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Green "Shawn Green") (2001), [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp") (2010), and [Joc Pederson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joc_Pederson "Joc Pederson") (2015).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-ocregister.com-37) He won the player of the week award as a result of that performance.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-38) He was also awarded with the [National League Player of the Month award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for April as he hit .383 with eight home runs and 19 RBI in the month.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-39) He recorded his 1,000th career RBI when he hit a two-run home run off [Julio Teherán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Teher%C3%A1n "Julio Teherán") of the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") on May 26.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-40) Gonzalez was selected to the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2015 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), the first Dodger first baseman selected since [Nomar Garciaparra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomar_Garciaparra "Nomar Garciaparra") in 2006.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-41) He finished the season by hitting .275 in 156 games with 28 home runs and 90 RBI, the lowest RBI total he had since 2006.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-br-42)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_%282%29.jpeg/250px-Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_%282%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_(2).jpeg)

González in 2016

González played for the [Mexico national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team") in the [World Baseball Classic qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic_%E2%80%93_Qualification "2017 World Baseball Classic – Qualification") during spring training in March 2016. The team was managed by his brother [Edgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-43) On June 22, 2016, during a game against the [Washington Nationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Nationals "Washington Nationals"), Gonzalez made a highlight-reel catch after a ball in foul territory deflected off [Chase Utley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Utley "Chase Utley")'s glove and off Gonzalez's leg.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-44) On August 7, he hit his 300th career home run against the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-45) On the season he appeared in 156 games, with a .285 batting average, 18 homers and 90 RBI. It was the fewest home runs he had hit in a season since 2012.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-46)

#### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2017")]

On May 5, 2017, González was placed on the 10-day [disabled list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_list "Disabled list") (DL) due to right elbow soreness. It was the first time in his MLB career that González was put on the DL.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-47) González recorded his 2,000th career hit with a double off [Johnny Barbato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Barbato "Johnny Barbato") of the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates "Pittsburgh Pirates") on August 22.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-49) González dealt with lingering back issues during the 2017 season, which caused him to spend half the season on the DL and lose playing time to rookie [Cody Bellinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Bellinger "Cody Bellinger") at first base. For the 2017 season, González only appeared in 71 games, batting .242/.287/.355 with 30 RBIs. He was shut down for the season in September and did not appear on the Dodgers playoff roster.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-50) In his final at-bat with the Dodgers, Gonzalez hit a home run against the Padres, giving him the rare distinction of having homered in both his first and last at-bats with the team.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-51)

On December 16, 2017, the Dodgers traded González, [Charlie Culberson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Culberson "Charlie Culberson"), [Scott Kazmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Kazmir "Scott Kazmir"), [Brandon McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_McCarthy "Brandon McCarthy"), and $4.5 million to the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") for [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-52) Immediately following the trade, the Braves designated González for assignment,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-53) then released him two days later.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-54) González waived his no-trade clause to facilitate the trade, which he did because he wanted to test [free agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agency_(Major_League_Baseball) "Free agency (Major League Baseball)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-55)

### New York Mets

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: New York Mets")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg/250px-Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg)

Gonzalez with the Mets in 2018

On January 18, 2018, González signed a one-year contract with the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-56) He was still due $21.5 million from his 2011 contract extension, with the Mets paying him $545,000 for the season.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-57)

On June 10, 2018, the Mets granted González his unconditional release. In 54 games with the Mets, he batted .237/.299/.373; he had just three hits in his final 27 at bats with the team.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-58)

### Mariachis de Guadalajara

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Mariachis de Guadalajara")]

On March 30, 2021, González announced his return to baseball and officially signed with the [Mariachis de Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariachis_de_Guadalajara "Mariachis de Guadalajara") of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League "Mexican Baseball League").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-59) On July 19, González announced that he would retire from professional baseball following the conclusion of the Mexican League season.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-60) In 43 games for Guadalajara, González batted .340/.412/.531 with 6 home runs and 41 RBI. He officially announced his retirement from professional baseball on February 5, 2022.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-l922-61)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

González and his wife Betsy reside in the San Diego County community of [La Jolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla,_California "La Jolla, California").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-62) They have two daughters.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-63) The couple created _The Adrián and Betsy González Foundation_, which is focused on empowering underprivileged youth in areas of athletics, education and health.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-64) As one of his charitable endeavors, González paid for the refurbishing of the baseball field in the Tijuana sports complex where he played as a youth.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)

González is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") and engraved on his bats is "PS 27:1" for verse 1 from [Psalm 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psalm_27 "Psalm 27").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-65) González has spoken about his faith saying, "I don't want to be remembered in baseball. I want to be remembered as a good witness for [Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus "Jesus"). ... I'm just trying to use this platform to bring people to Christ."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-66)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Mexican-American baseball player (born 1982)

This article is about the baseball player. For other people, see [Adrián González (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_(disambiguation) "Adrián González (disambiguation)").

In this [Spanish name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_name "Spanish name"), the first or paternal[surname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surname "Surname") is _González_ and the second or maternal family name is _Savín_.

**Adrián González Savín** (born May 8, 1982), also known by his nicknames "**A-Gon**" and "**Titán**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-1) is a Mexican-American former professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball")[first baseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_baseman "First baseman"). He played in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB) for the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"), [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres"), [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox"), [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), and [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").

González was born in the United States, but was raised in [Tijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana "Tijuana"), Baja California, Mexico, until 1990, when he returned to the United States. He played for [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team") in the [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Baseball_Classic "2006 World Baseball Classic"), [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Baseball_Classic "2009 World Baseball Classic"), [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Baseball_Classic "2013 World Baseball Classic"), and the [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic "2017 World Baseball Classic") editions of the [World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Baseball_Classic "World Baseball Classic") and the [2020 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Baseball at the 2020 Summer Olympics").

González was the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_Major_League_Baseball_draft_picks "List of first overall Major League Baseball draft picks") in the [2000 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2000 Major League Baseball draft") by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins"). He was traded to the Rangers, and made his MLB debut with them in 2004. He was traded to the Padres after the 2005 season, where he was an [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "Major League Baseball All-Star Game") selection three times and a two-time [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawlings_Gold_Glove_Award "Rawlings Gold Glove Award") winner. He was traded to the Red Sox after the 2010 season, and was traded to the Dodgers in August 2012. After playing for the Dodgers throughout the 2017 season, he was traded to the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves"), but was released without playing for them. He then played for the Mets, who released him during the 2018 season.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Adrián González was born in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California, to David and Alba González, both Mexican natives.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-3) González is the youngest of three boys; his brothers are David Jr. and [Edgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)"), a former big leaguer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-little-4) After his birth, his parents moved the family to [Tijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana "Tijuana"), where his father owned an air-conditioner business.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2) The three boys grew up playing baseball in Mexico,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2) where their father had been a member of the [Mexico national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5) In 1990, the family returned to the United States, settling in [Bonita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonita,_California "Bonita, California").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5)

While Adrián was drafted by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins") out of high school, his brother [Edgar Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)") attended [San Diego State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_State_University "San Diego State University") and was selected by the [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays") in the 30th round of the 2000 draft.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5) Edgar debuted in the major leagues as a utility man with the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") in 2008, joining his brother as a teammate.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-6)

In 2012, David and Alba González were named George and Barbara Bush Little League Parents of the Year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-little-4) In November 2012, González was honored as one of 30 "exemplary citizens" by the mayor of Tijuana in an official ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)

González was projected to be a late first-round pick out of [Eastlake High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastlake_High_School_(Chula_Vista,_California) "Eastlake High School (Chula Vista, California)") in [Chula Vista, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chula_Vista,_California "Chula Vista, California");[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-8) however, his stock increased with his senior-year performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-9) In his senior year, he hit .645 with 13 home runs and 34 runs batted in.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-10)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Florida Marlins (2000–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Florida Marlins (2000–2003)")]

In June 2000, González became the first infield position player to be drafted first overall since [Alex Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Rodriguez "Alex Rodriguez") in 1993. He was given a $3 million signing bonus by the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-11) While in the Marlins organization, González played with the [Gulf Coast League Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_League_Marlins "Gulf Coast League Marlins"), [Kane County Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kane_County_Cougars "Kane County Cougars"), [Utica Blue Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica_Blue_Sox "Utica Blue Sox"), [Portland Sea Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Sea_Dogs "Portland Sea Dogs") (2002),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-12)[Albuquerque Isotopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Isotopes "Albuquerque Isotopes") (2003), and [Carolina Mudcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Mudcats_(1991%E2%80%932011) "Carolina Mudcats (1991–2011)") (2003). With the Single-A Kane County Cougars in his second professional season, González hit .312 with 17 home runs and 103 RBIs in 127 games. As a result, he was selected by the [Midwest League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League "Midwest League") as its [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Midwest League Most Valuable Player Award") and [Prospect of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_League_Prospect_of_the_Year_Award "Midwest League Prospect of the Year Award"). He also played in the [All-Star Futures Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Futures_Game "All-Star Futures Game").

### Texas Rangers (2004–2005)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Texas Rangers (2004–2005)")]

After a wrist injury, the Marlins felt González would be hindered swinging the bat, so they included González in a June 2003 trade with the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"), along with [Ryan Snare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Snare "Ryan Snare") and minor leaguer Will Smith, to acquire relief pitcher [Ugueth Urbina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugueth_Urbina "Ugueth Urbina") to aid their championship drive.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-13) González played with the Rangers' Class-AA team, the [Frisco RoughRiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisco_RoughRiders "Frisco RoughRiders"), until he made his major-league debut against the [Seattle Mariners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Mariners "Seattle Mariners") on April 18, 2004. He was hitless in three at-bats. He recorded his first base hit on April 20 against [Ramón Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Ortiz "Ramón Ortiz") of the [Anaheim Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Angels "Anaheim Angels") and his first home run on April 25 off [Kevin Jarvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Jarvis "Kevin Jarvis") of the Seattle Mariners. He played in 16 games for Texas in 2004 and in 43 games in 2005, with a combined batting average of .229 and 7 homers.

### San Diego Padres (2006–2010)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: San Diego Padres (2006–2010)")]

#### 2006

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2006")]

After the season, González was traded to the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") along with pitcher [Chris Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Young_(pitcher) "Chris Young (pitcher)") and [outfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outfielder "Outfielder")[Terrmel Sledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrmel_Sledge "Terrmel Sledge"). In return, the Rangers received [Adam Eaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Eaton_(pitcher) "Adam Eaton (pitcher)") and [Akinori Otsuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akinori_Otsuka "Akinori Otsuka"). Originally seen as an eventual replacement for [Ryan Klesko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Klesko "Ryan Klesko") at first base, González was given the job when Klesko underwent shoulder surgery.

With extended playing time at first base in 2006, González continued to improve his hitting and defense. On July 23, 2006, he was named the [NL Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NL_Player_of_the_Week "NL Player of the Week").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-14) In his first full season, he led the Padres in [batting average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") (.304) and [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") (24). He was the first player in [Petco Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petco_Park "Petco Park") history to have more than one multiple home run game. He was named the Padres MVP for 2006.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2007

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2007")]

On March 31, 2007, González agreed to a $9.5 million, four-year deal, with a club option for $5.5 million in 2011.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-16) In the 2007 season, he led the Padres in home runs again, with 30, and had a team-high 100 RBIs. He led all Major League first basemen with 161 games and a career-high 46 doubles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2008

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2008")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg/330px-Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_01.jpg)

González after a swing with the [Padres in 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_San_Diego_Padres_season "2008 San Diego Padres season")

In the 2008 season, González finished with a .279 average and once again led the Padres with 36 home runs and 119 RBIs. He was elected to the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2008 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") as a reserve. In the exhibition, he went 1 for 3 with a single and a sacrifice fly, driving in [Miguel Tejada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Tejada "Miguel Tejada"). He won his first [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Glove_Award "Gold Glove Award") in 2008 at first base and set career highs in games played (162), home runs (36), RBI (119), runs scored (103), walks (74), and slugging percentage (.510). He was named the Padres MVP for the second time.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2009

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2009")]

González played winter ball in the [Mexican Pacific League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Pacific_League "Mexican Pacific League") with the [Venados de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venados_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Venados de Mazatlán"). In the [Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Caribbean_Series "2009 Caribbean Series"), he led his team past the Dominican Republic's [Tigres del Licey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigres_del_Licey "Tigres del Licey") with a record-setting 3 home runs on February 4.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-17)

González hit 23 homers, leading the majors in that category through May 2009 despite playing his home games at Petco Park, which Padres statisticians describe as an "extreme [pitcher's park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitcher's_park "Pitcher's park")."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb.mlb.com-18) On May 18, González was described as being one of the two most underrated players in the National League according to an [MLB.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB.com "MLB.com") poll of major league executives and managers.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlb.mlb.com-18) On June 1, he was named the NL Co-[Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") for the second time in his career. During that week, González hit four home runs, tallied 10 RBIs, and had a 1.000 slugging percentage.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-19) González was elected to the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2009 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") after voting by fellow players, managers and coaches.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-20) He subsequently participated in that year's [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby "Home Run Derby"), where he hit two home runs in the first round. On August 1, González batted 6-for-6 with three [RBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in") as the Padres topped the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") 13–6. González's six hits are the most by any Padre in a nine-inning game. Three others have accomplished the feat, but did it in extra-inning contests. González hit five singles and a double.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-21)

He led the majors in walks in 2009 with 119[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-22) and set a major league record with eight consecutive multi-walk games,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-23) a record which still stands as of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-24) He also hit 40 home runs for the first time in his career. He was named the Padres team MVP for 2009, his third time honored.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-mlbbio-15)

#### 2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2010")]

González started the 2010 season playing well. On May 24, he was named the NL Player of the Week for the fourth time in his career.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-25) On June 2, González hit a [walk-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk-off_home_run "Walk-off home run")[grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_(baseball) "Grand slam (baseball)") in the eleventh inning of a 5–1 victory over the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-26) In July, González was elected to participate in his third consecutive [All-Star game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2010 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").

During the 2010 season, González had 176 hits in 591 at-bats, good for a .298 batting average, his highest since hitting .304 in 2006. His 93 walks put him in third place in the NL behind only [Prince Fielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Fielder "Prince Fielder") (114) and [Albert Pujols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Pujols "Albert Pujols") (103). He finished with 31 home runs and 101 RBI, the third time in his career he had 100 RBI or more. González played in 160 games on the year, tying him with [Rickie Weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickie_Weeks "Rickie Weeks") for 5th in the NL. He scored 87 runs on the season, compiling 302 [total bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_base "Total base"), which also tied him with Weeks, for 6th in the NL. González was named team MVP for the third consecutive year and the fourth time overall with the Padres.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-27)

### Boston Red Sox (2011–2012)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Boston Red Sox (2011–2012)")]

On December 6, 2010, González was traded to the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox") for a package of right-handed pitcher [Casey Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Kelly "Casey Kelly"), first baseman [Anthony Rizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Rizzo "Anthony Rizzo"), outfielder [Reymond Fuentes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reymond_Fuentes "Reymond Fuentes"), and a [player to be named later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_to_be_named_later "Player to be named later"), later determined to be [Eric Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Patterson_(baseball) "Eric Patterson (baseball)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-29)

On April 15, 2011, González and the Red Sox agreed to a seven-year contract extension worth $154 million through the 2018 season.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-30) On June 19, González hit his 1,000th career hit: a triple off of [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") pitcher [Yovani Gallardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yovani_Gallardo "Yovani Gallardo").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-l452-31)

On July 3, 2011, González was selected to the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2011 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") in Arizona along with teammates [Josh Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Beckett "Josh Beckett"), [Jacoby Ellsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacoby_Ellsbury "Jacoby Ellsbury"), [David Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ortiz "David Ortiz"), [Kevin Youkilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Youkilis "Kevin Youkilis"), and [Jon Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Lester "Jon Lester"). González hit a home run in the game and was responsible for the only run for the [American League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_League "American League"). Additionally, Ortiz selected González as one of three sluggers to join him in the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby "Home Run Derby"), where he finished second to [Robinson Canó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robinson_Can%C3%B3 "Robinson Canó"). González tied a record for most home runs in the final round of the home run derby at 11, which was then surpassed by the victor Canó.

González was named AL [Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for June 2011 with a .404 average (40 for 99) – the best in the Majors for that month.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-32) After placing second in the [2011 Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Major_League_Baseball_Home_Run_Derby "2011 Major League Baseball Home Run Derby"), González faced a home-run slump until he hit five home runs in ten at-bats on August 23–25.

On November 21, González finished seventh in MVP voting, trailing his teammate Ellsbury in second and the winner, [Detroit Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Tigers "Detroit Tigers") ace [Justin Verlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Verlander "Justin Verlander").

González appeared on the cover of baseball video game _[MLB 12: The Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB\_12:\_The\_Show "MLB 12: The Show")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-33) In 2012, González appeared in 123 games with the Red Sox, hitting .300 with 15 homers and 86 RBI.

### Los Angeles Dodgers (2012–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Los Angeles Dodgers (2012–2017)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21%2C_2013.jpg/250px-Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21%2C_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_on_April_21,_2013.jpg)

González in 2013

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2012")]

On August 25, 2012, González was traded to the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers") (along with [Josh Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Beckett "Josh Beckett"), [Nick Punto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Punto "Nick Punto") and [Carl Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Crawford "Carl Crawford")) and $11 million in cash for [James Loney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Loney "James Loney"), [Iván DeJesús Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iv%C3%A1n_DeJes%C3%BAs_Jr. "Iván DeJesús Jr."), [Allen Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Webster_(baseball) "Allen Webster (baseball)") and two players to be named later ([Jerry Sands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Sands "Jerry Sands") and [Rubby De La Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubby_De_La_Rosa "Rubby De La Rosa")).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-34) In his first at bat with the Dodgers that same day, he hit a three-run home run against the [Miami Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Marlins "Miami Marlins").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-35) In 36 games with the Dodgers, he hit .297 with 3 homers and 22 RBI.

#### 2013

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2013")]

In the 2013 season, González appeared in 157 games for the Dodgers and hit .293 with 22 home runs and 100 RBI. He was a candidate for the [final vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Final_Vote "All-Star Final Vote") at the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2013 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") but was not chosen for the game.

In Game 5 of the [NLCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_National_League_Championship_Series "2013 National League Championship Series") against the [St. Louis Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals"), González went 3 for 4 with 2 home runs. The Dodgers would eventually lose the series in six games.

#### 2014

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2014")]

González finished the 2014 season with 116 RBI, most in the majors. He was the Dodgers' nominee for the [Hank Aaron Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Aaron_Award "Hank Aaron Award"), after hitting 27 home runs in 159 games. However, his batting average of .276 was the lowest of his career. He finished up the season by winning the [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award") for NL first baseman and also won several awards for his defense at first base, including the [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Glove_Award "Gold Glove Award"), [Fielding Bible Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_Bible_Award "Fielding Bible Award") and [Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Sporting_Goods "Wilson Sporting Goods").

#### 2015

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: 2015")]

González opened the 2015 season with five home runs in the first three games of the season, including three on April 8 against [Andrew Cashner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cashner "Andrew Cashner"). He was the first MLB player to hit five home runs in the first three games of the season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-36) By homering in his fifth consecutive game, dating back to the end of the 2014 season, he tied the team record, which he shares with [Roy Campanella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Campanella "Roy Campanella") (1950), [Shawn Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Green "Shawn Green") (2001), [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp") (2010), and [Joc Pederson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joc_Pederson "Joc Pederson") (2015).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-ocregister.com-37) He won the player of the week award as a result of that performance.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-38) He was also awarded with the [National League Player of the Month award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for April as he hit .383 with eight home runs and 19 RBI in the month.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-39) He recorded his 1,000th career RBI when he hit a two-run home run off [Julio Teherán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Teher%C3%A1n "Julio Teherán") of the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") on May 26.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-40) Gonzalez was selected to the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2015 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), the first Dodger first baseman selected since [Nomar Garciaparra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomar_Garciaparra "Nomar Garciaparra") in 2006.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-41) He finished the season by hitting .275 in 156 games with 28 home runs and 90 RBI, the lowest RBI total he had since 2006.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-br-42)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_%282%29.jpeg/250px-Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_%282%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrian_Gonzalez_during_game_against_Yankees_9-13-16_(2).jpeg)

González in 2016

González played for the [Mexico national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team") in the [World Baseball Classic qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic_%E2%80%93_Qualification "2017 World Baseball Classic – Qualification") during spring training in March 2016. The team was managed by his brother [Edgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Gonzalez_(infielder) "Edgar Gonzalez (infielder)").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-43) On June 22, 2016, during a game against the [Washington Nationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Nationals "Washington Nationals"), Gonzalez made a highlight-reel catch after a ball in foul territory deflected off [Chase Utley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Utley "Chase Utley")'s glove and off Gonzalez's leg.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-44) On August 7, he hit his 300th career home run against the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-45) On the season he appeared in 156 games, with a .285 batting average, 18 homers and 90 RBI. It was the fewest home runs he had hit in a season since 2012.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-46)

#### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2017")]

On May 5, 2017, González was placed on the 10-day [disabled list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_list "Disabled list") (DL) due to right elbow soreness. It was the first time in his MLB career that González was put on the DL.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-47) González recorded his 2,000th career hit with a double off [Johnny Barbato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Barbato "Johnny Barbato") of the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates "Pittsburgh Pirates") on August 22.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-49) González dealt with lingering back issues during the 2017 season, which caused him to spend half the season on the DL and lose playing time to rookie [Cody Bellinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Bellinger "Cody Bellinger") at first base. For the 2017 season, González only appeared in 71 games, batting .242/.287/.355 with 30 RBIs. He was shut down for the season in September and did not appear on the Dodgers playoff roster.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-50) In his final at-bat with the Dodgers, Gonzalez hit a home run against the Padres, giving him the rare distinction of having homered in both his first and last at-bats with the team.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-51)

On December 16, 2017, the Dodgers traded González, [Charlie Culberson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Culberson "Charlie Culberson"), [Scott Kazmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Kazmir "Scott Kazmir"), [Brandon McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_McCarthy "Brandon McCarthy"), and $4.5 million to the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") for [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-52) Immediately following the trade, the Braves designated González for assignment,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-53) then released him two days later.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-54) González waived his no-trade clause to facilitate the trade, which he did because he wanted to test [free agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agency_(Major_League_Baseball) "Free agency (Major League Baseball)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-55)

### New York Mets

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: New York Mets")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg/250px-Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez_in_2018.jpg)

Gonzalez with the Mets in 2018

On January 18, 2018, González signed a one-year contract with the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-56) He was still due $21.5 million from his 2011 contract extension, with the Mets paying him $545,000 for the season.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-57)

On June 10, 2018, the Mets granted González his unconditional release. In 54 games with the Mets, he batted .237/.299/.373; he had just three hits in his final 27 at bats with the team.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-58)

### Mariachis de Guadalajara

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Mariachis de Guadalajara")]

On March 30, 2021, González announced his return to baseball and officially signed with the [Mariachis de Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariachis_de_Guadalajara "Mariachis de Guadalajara") of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League "Mexican Baseball League").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-59) On July 19, González announced that he would retire from professional baseball following the conclusion of the Mexican League season.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-60) In 43 games for Guadalajara, González batted .340/.412/.531 with 6 home runs and 41 RBI. He officially announced his retirement from professional baseball on February 5, 2022.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-l922-61)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

González and his wife Betsy reside in the San Diego County community of [La Jolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla,_California "La Jolla, California").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-62) They have two daughters.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-63) The couple created _The Adrián and Betsy González Foundation_, which is focused on empowering underprivileged youth in areas of athletics, education and health.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-64) As one of his charitable endeavors, González paid for the refurbishing of the baseball field in the Tijuana sports complex where he played as a youth.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-lat-2)

González is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") and engraved on his bats is "PS 27:1" for verse 1 from [Psalm 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psalm_27 "Psalm 27").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-65) González has spoken about his faith saying, "I don't want to be remembered in baseball. I want to be remembered as a good witness for [Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus "Jesus"). ... I'm just trying to use this platform to bring people to Christ."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Gonz%C3%A1lez#cite_note-66)
