**Andrew Stefan McCutchen** (born October 10, 1986)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-gaz1-1) is an American professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball")[outfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outfielder "Outfielder") and [designated hitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Designated_hitter "Designated hitter") who is a free agent. He has previously played in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB) for the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates "Pittsburgh Pirates"), [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants"), [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees"), [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies "Philadelphia Phillies"), [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers"), and [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"). Internationally, McCutchen [represents the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_baseball_team "United States national baseball team"). In the [2017 World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic "2017 World Baseball Classic") (WBC), he helped win Team USA's first [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") in a WBC tournament.

The Pirates selected McCutchen in the first round (11th pick overall) of the [2005 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2005 Major League Baseball draft"), and he made his MLB debut in 2009. During McCutchen's first tenure in Pittsburgh, he was the [National League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_League_(baseball) "National League (baseball)") (NL) [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award") in 2013, a five-time [All Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "Major League Baseball All-Star Game") (2011–2015), a four-time [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award") winner (2012–2015), a [Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Glove_Award "Gold Glove Award") winner in 2012, and the [Roberto Clemente Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente_Award "Roberto Clemente Award") winner in 2015. McCutchen led the NL in [hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_(baseball) "Hit (baseball)") (194) in 2012, and in [on-base percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_percentage "On-base percentage") (.410), [OPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_plus_slugging "On-base plus slugging") (.952), and [extra base hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_base_hit "Extra base hit") (69) in 2014.

## Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early years")]

McCutchen was born in [Fort Meade, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Meade,_Florida "Fort Meade, Florida"), to Lorenzo McCutchen and Petrina Swan, who were high school teenagers at the time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-2) He has a sister, Loren.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He lived with his mother while his father attended [Carson–Newman University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carson%E2%80%93Newman_University "Carson–Newman University") in [Jefferson City, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_City,_Tennessee "Jefferson City, Tennessee"), where Lorenzo played [running back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_back "Running back") on the [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") team.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-3) Lorenzo gave up his dream of making the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) to be close to his son and returned to Fort Meade in 1989.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-4) Petrina would not marry him unless he became a church minister, which he did.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The two married on August 1, 1992.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-gaz1-1)

McCutchen was eligible to play [varsity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varsity_team "Varsity team") baseball as an eighth grader at [Fort Meade High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Meade_High_School "Fort Meade High School").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-5) He [batted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") .591 as a freshman.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-6) McCutchen's average his senior season was .709, as he hit 16 [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") and 42 [runs batted in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_batted_in "Runs batted in") (RBIs).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-7) During his varsity career, McCutchen batted .474.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-nbc-8)

McCutchen also ran [track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field "Track and field") and played football.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-9) He was part of a state title-winning [4 × 100 metres relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_%C3%97_100_metres_relay "4 × 100 metres relay") in his first year of high school.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-10) McCutchen was one of the top 200 football recruits in the state of Florida, with his high school position being [wide receiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_receiver "Wide receiver"), but opted for a baseball career.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-11) He was reportedly offered a full-ride scholarship to the [University of Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Miami "University of Miami") to play football.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-12)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Draft and minor leagues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Draft and minor leagues")]

McCutchen, who had committed to the [University of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florida "University of Florida"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-13) was drafted 11th overall by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the first round of the [2005 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2005 Major League Baseball draft").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-14) He signed with the Pirates, receiving a $1.9 million [signing bonus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signing_bonus "Signing bonus"), instead of attending Florida.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-gaz2-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) In 2005, he played for the Rookie [Gulf Coast League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_League "Gulf Coast League") (GCL) [Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCL_Pirates "GCL Pirates") and the Single–A [Williamsport Crosscutters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsport_Crosscutters "Williamsport Crosscutters"), and hit a combined .310/.419 (2nd in the GCL)/.433 with two home runs and 17 stolen bases in 210 at-bats, as he was second in the league with 29 walks, tied for second with 36 runs, third with three triples, and fifth with 13 stolen bases.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference-GCL-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-circle-18)

Before the 2006 season _[Baseball America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball\_America "Baseball America")_ named McCutchen the #50 prospect in the minor leagues.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) McCutchen played the majority of the season for the Single-A [Hickory Crawdads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickory_Crawdads "Hickory Crawdads"), for whom he started the [South Atlantic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Atlantic_League "South Atlantic League") (SAL) All-Star team in his first full season as a [professional player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_baseball "Professional baseball") and was a postseason SAL All-Star.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-square-19)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-20) He also played for the Double-A [Altoona Curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altoona_Curve "Altoona Curve") and batted a combined .294/.359/.450 with 17 home runs and 23 stolen bases in 531 at-bats.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference-SAL-21) At the end of that year, the Pirates named him the organization's Minor League Player of the Year.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-eagle-22)

Before the 2007 season _Baseball America_ named McCutchen the #13 prospect in the minor leagues, and _[Baseball Prospectus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball\_Prospectus "Baseball Prospectus")_ named him the #15 prospect.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) He played again for Altoona, as well as for the Triple-A [Indianapolis Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Indians "Indianapolis Indians"), and hit a combined .265/.329/.388 with 11 home runs and 21 stolen bases in 513 at bats.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) In 2007 he also played for the [Phoenix Desert Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Desert_Dogs "Phoenix Desert Dogs"), he was on the [Arizona Fall League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Fall_League "Arizona Fall League") All-Prospect Team and named a Rising Star.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-circle-18)

Before the 2008 season _Baseball America_ named him the #14 prospect in the minor leagues, and _Baseball Prospectus_ named him the #24 prospect.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) In 2008, McCutchen was a mid-season [International League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_League "International League") (IL) All-Star, an [All-Star Futures Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Futures_Game "All-Star Futures Game") selection, and the Triple-A All-Star Game Top Star.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-circle-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-square-19) He played the entire season with Indianapolis, and batted .283/.372 (10th in the IL)/.398 with 12 home runs, 68 walks (3rd in the league), 34 stolen bases (7th), and 145 hits (9th), in 512 at-bats.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16)

Before the 2009 season _Baseball America_ named McCutchen the #33 prospect in the minor leagues, and _Baseball Prospectus_ named him the #25 prospect.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16) He again played for Indianapolis, but played only 49 games for them, as he batted .303/.361/.493 with 4 home runs and 17 stolen bases in 201 at-bats.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference2-16)

### Pittsburgh Pirates (2009–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pittsburgh Pirates (2009–2017)")]

#### 2009

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2009")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/DSCN1076_Andrew_McCutchen.jpg/250px-DSCN1076_Andrew_McCutchen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DSCN1076_Andrew_McCutchen.jpg)

McCutchen in 2009

On June 3, 2009, after the Pittsburgh Pirates traded starting center fielder [Nate McLouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_McLouth "Nate McLouth") to the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves"), McCutchen was called up to MLB for the first time.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-23) He made his MLB debut the next day, playing center field and batting [leadoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadoff_hitter "Leadoff hitter") against the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets"). He [singled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_(baseball) "Single (baseball)") in his first career [at-bat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At_bat "At bat"), off starter [Mike Pelfrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pelfrey "Mike Pelfrey").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-24) McCutchen ended the day with two singles, one RBI, three [runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_(baseball) "Run (baseball)") scored, and a [stolen base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolen_base "Stolen base") in four at-bats.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-25) He recorded his first career four-hit game five days later, against McLouth and the Braves.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-26) Two of his hits were [triples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_(baseball) "Triple (baseball)"), making him the first Pirate with two triples in a game since [Tike Redman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tike_Redman "Tike Redman") accomplished the feat in 2003.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-27)

On June 17, McCutchen hit his first MLB career home run off of [Francisco Liriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Liriano "Francisco Liriano") of the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins "Minnesota Twins").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-28) On June 25, he had his first MLB career walk-off hit, off [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians") closer [Matt Herges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Herges "Matt Herges").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-29) "He's an impressive-looking young player. He really is," said Indians manager [Eric Wedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Wedge "Eric Wedge").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-30)

On August 1, against the [Washington Nationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Nationals "Washington Nationals"), McCutchen went 4-for-5, with three home runs and six RBIs.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-31) He became the 10th Pirates player ever to hit three home runs in a single game, and the first one to do it during his rookie year.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-gaz3-32) Ten days later against the [Colorado Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies "Colorado Rockies") at [Coors Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Field "Coors Field"), he stole a career-high three bases in a game off three different Rockies pitchers.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-33) McCutchen hit his first walk-off home run on August 25, off [Brad Lidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Lidge "Brad Lidge") of the [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies "Philadelphia Phillies").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-34)

McCutchen finished his rookie season batting .286/.365/.471, with nine triples (sixth in the National League), an 81.48 [stolen base percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolen_base_percentage "Stolen base percentage") (6th), 12 home runs, 54 RBIs, and 22 stolen bases in 108 games.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he had 10 [assists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assist_(baseball) "Assist (baseball)") (third among NL center fielders), and a 2.53 [range factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_factor "Range factor")/game (4th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

McCutchen finished fourth in the voting for the [National League Rookie of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "Major League Baseball Rookie of the Year Award"), behind [Chris Coghlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Coghlan "Chris Coghlan"), [J. A. Happ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._A._Happ "J. A. Happ"), and [Tommy Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Hanson "Tommy Hanson").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-36) He was named the [Baseball America Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_America_Rookie_of_the_Year "Baseball America Rookie of the Year") for 2009.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-37)

#### 2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010")]

McCutchen began the 2010 season as the Pirates' everyday center fielder.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-38) "He's an All-Star. This year, probably," said Atlanta Braves manager [Bobby Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cox "Bobby Cox"); "Hitting. Running. Defense. Throwing. He's got it all. He catches the ball like [Andruw Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andruw_Jones "Andruw Jones") did when he was 19. You can't hit a ball [past him] out there. He's got lightning in that bat too."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-39)

McCutchen posted a career day against the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") on May 14, going 5-for-5 with five runs scored in a 10–7 Pirates win.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-40) Teammate [Garrett Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrett_Jones "Garrett Jones") also recorded five hits, making McCutchen and Jones the first Pirate duo since [Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Baseball_Hall_of_Fame_and_Museum "National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum") inductee [Willie Stargell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Stargell "Willie Stargell") and [Bob Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Robertson "Bob Robertson") accomplished the feat in 1970.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-41) "I guess we were just kind of competing against each other," McCutchen said, laughing. "I don't know. I'd get a hit, he'd get a hit. He'd hit a homer, I'd hit a homer."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-42) McCutchen finished the month of May with career-best numbers, hitting .327 with a .901 [OPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_plus_slugging "On-base plus slugging"), which drew comparisons with [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays")[All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "Major League Baseball All-Star Game")[Carl Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Crawford "Carl Crawford").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-43)

McCutchen was not named to the 2010 National League All-Star Team.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-44) Pirates pitcher [Evan Meek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Meek "Evan Meek"), who was named the Pirates representative, said that McCutchen was "very deserving" and should have gone as well.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-45)

After hitting .226 in August, McCutchen batted .326, with 22 runs and 15 RBIs, in September; he also recorded 12 multi-hit games from September 3 – October 3.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-46) McCutchen said about the changes from August to September, "Honestly, I don't think I'm doing anything any different right now. You swing, and the ball finds a hole. That's it. That's the game of baseball."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-47)

McCutchen finished his second major league season hitting .286/.365/.449 while adding 94 runs, 16 home runs, 56 RBIs, and 33 stolen bases (5th in the National League), with a 21.6 [power-speed number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power-speed_number "Power-speed number") (9th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he had 8 assists (3rd of all NL center fielders) and 2 [double plays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_play "Double play") from center field (5th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

#### 2011

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2011")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Andrew_McCutchen_2011.jpg/250px-Andrew_McCutchen_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_2011.jpg)

McCutchen in 2011

McCutchen took the place of the injured [Ryan Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Braun "Ryan Braun") as a member of the National League [All Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Star "All Star") team at the [2011 Major League Baseball All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2011 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") in Phoenix.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-48) On August 30, 2011, McCutchen hit a ninth-inning homer against the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros") to become the eighth Pirates player to record at least 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases in one season.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He was the first Pirate to accomplish the feat since [Nate McLouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_McLouth "Nate McLouth") in 2008.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-49)

McCutchen finished the season batting .259/.364/.456 with team highs of 23 home runs, 23 stolen bases, 87 runs, and 89 RBIs.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-50) He also had a 23.0 power-speed number (4th in the National League) and 89 [walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk "Walk") (5th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he led all NL outfielders in [putouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Putout "Putout") (414), double plays (5), and range factor/game (2.73).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He was nominated as the Pirates' representative for the [Hank Aaron Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Aaron_Award "Hank Aaron Award").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-51)

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2012")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Andrew_McCutchen_on_June_12%2C_2012.jpg/250px-Andrew_McCutchen_on_June_12%2C_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_on_June_12,_2012.jpg)

McCutchen in 2012

On March 5, 2012, McCutchen signed a six-year, $51.5 million contract extension with the Pirates, with a $14.75 million club option for 2018.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-52) He was a [2012 NL All Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_MLB_All-Star_Game "2012 MLB All-Star Game").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-53) McCutchen was chosen to replace [Giancarlo Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giancarlo_Stanton "Giancarlo Stanton") in the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby "Home Run Derby") due to injury.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-54) He hit 4 home runs during the first round of the competition, and failed to reach the second round.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-55)

McCutchen was named [NL Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for June, his first selection.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-Player-56) He won his first [NL Player of the Week Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") on July 8, and later won it a second consecutive week on July 15, becoming the first Pirate since [Jason Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bay "Jason Bay") in 2006 to do so.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-Player-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-57) During July he hit .446 with seven home runs and 15 RBIs and was named the NL Player of the Month for a second consecutive month.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He became the first Pirate since [Bobby Bonilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Bonilla "Bobby Bonilla") during the [1988 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Pittsburgh_Pirates_season "1988 Pittsburgh Pirates season") to earn the award twice in the same season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-58)

McCutchen finished the season batting .327 (2nd in the NL)/.400 (3rd)/.553 (3rd), led the NL with 194 [hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_(baseball) "Hit (baseball)") and 269 [times on base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_on_base "Times on base"), scored 107 runs (2nd), had 128 singles (2nd), had a 24.3 power-speed number (4th), drew 13 [intentional walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intentional_walk "Intentional walk") (5th), hit 31 home runs (8th), and drew 70 walks (8th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He stole 20 bases, marking his fourth consecutive season of 20 or more on the season.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-59) On defense, he had a .997 [fielding percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_percentage "Fielding percentage") (2nd-best among NL outfielders), and a 2.37 range factor/game (4th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

McCutchen finished third in the NL [Most Valuable Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Most Valuable Player Award") voting, behind San Francisco's [Buster Posey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buster_Posey "Buster Posey") and Milwaukee's [Ryan Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Braun "Ryan Braun").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-60) McCutchen was voted the Player's Choice National League Outstanding Player.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-61) He also won his first [Louisville Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Silver_Slugger_Award "Louisville Silver Slugger Award") as the top offensive center fielder in baseball, won a [Rawlings Gold Glove Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawlings_Gold_Glove_Award "Rawlings Gold Glove Award"), and was named a 2012 NL [Wilson Defensive Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award") in the outfield.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

#### 2013: MVP season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2013: MVP season")]

In 2013, McCutchen was the athlete featured on the cover of the baseball video game _[MLB 13: The Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB\_13:\_The\_Show "MLB 13: The Show")_.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-62) He received 108,147 votes in a week of fan voting via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") and [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), while New York Yankees' pitcher [CC Sabathia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CC_Sabathia "CC Sabathia") came in second with 89,054 votes.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-63) Though athletes cannot appear twice on the cover, he appeared on the back cover of the 2014 edition of the game.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-trib-64)

On April 3, 2013, McCutchen stole his 100th career base.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-65) On September 3, 2013, facing [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") pitcher [Yovani Gallardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yovani_Gallardo "Yovani Gallardo"), he hit his 100th career home run.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-66)

McCutchen was named to the [2013 NL All-Star Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_MLB_All-Star_Game "2013 MLB All-Star Game"), becoming an All-Star for the third straight year as a reserve.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-67)

McCutchen finished the 2013 regular season batting .317 (7th in the National League)/.404 (3rd)/.508 (6th), with 185 hits and a 23.6 power-speed number (third), 78 walks and 12 intentional walks (4th), 97 runs (6th), 121 singles and 38 doubles (7th), 21 home runs, 84 RBIs, and 27 stolen bases (6th), which marked the fifth straight year he stole 20 or more bases.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he led all NL center fielders with three double plays and was third with 11 assists.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) His efforts helped lead Pittsburgh to a winning record and the postseason for the first time since the [1992 Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Pittsburgh_Pirates_season "1992 Pittsburgh Pirates season") team, led by [Barry Bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Bonds "Barry Bonds").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-68) They were eliminated by the [St. Louis Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals") in the [NLDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NLDS "2013 NLDS") in game 5.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-69)

McCutchen won the [National League MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_League_MVP "National League MVP") over Arizona's [Paul Goldschmidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Goldschmidt "Paul Goldschmidt") and St. Louis' [Yadier Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yadier_Molina "Yadier Molina"), becoming the first Pirate to win the award since Bonds in 1992.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-70) He also won his second [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award"), and his second NL Most Outstanding Player Award.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-72)

#### 2014

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2014")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/McclutchionPirates2014.jpg/250px-McclutchionPirates2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McclutchionPirates2014.jpg)

McCutchen batting in 2014 against the St. Louis Cardinals

On June 15, 2014, McCutchen won the NL Player of the Week Award, and in June 2014, he won the NL Player of the Month Award.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On the [4th of July](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States) "Independence Day (United States)") in 2014, against the [in-state rival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillies%E2%80%93Pirates_rivalry "Phillies–Pirates rivalry") Philadelphia Phillies, McCutchen came close to [hitting for the cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitting_for_the_cycle "Hitting for the cycle") by hitting 4-for-5 with two RBIs, barely missing a home run in the 8th inning when it hit the right field wall of [PNC Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNC_Park "PNC Park") a few feet short of clearing it.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-73) On July 13, he again won the NL Player of the Week Award.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On September 10, McCutchen hit his first career [inside-the-park homer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside-the-park_homer "Inside-the-park homer") against the Phillies.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-74)

McCutchen was elected to the All-Star Game for the fourth time.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-75) He made his first All-Star Game start.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-76)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Andrew_McCutchen%2C_April_2014.JPG/250px-Andrew_McCutchen%2C_April_2014.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen,_April_2014.JPG)

McCutchen in 2014

For the 2014 season, McCutchen batted .314 (3rd in the National League)/.410 (leading the league)/.542 (2nd in the league) with a .952 OPS (leading the league).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He had 69 [extra base hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_base_hit "Extra base hit") (leading the league), 297 [total bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_bases "Total bases") (2nd), 84 walks (4th), an 85.71 stolen base percentage (5th), a 20.9 power-speed number (6th), 38 [doubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(baseball) "Double (baseball)") (7th), 25 home runs (8th), 89 runs (10th), 8 intentional walks (10th), 18 stolen bases, and 83 RBIs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

McCutchen was awarded his third consecutive Silver Slugger for NL outfielders.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-77) He came in third in the voting for National League MVP, behind [Clayton Kershaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton_Kershaw "Clayton Kershaw") and [Giancarlo Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giancarlo_Stanton "Giancarlo Stanton").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

#### 2015

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2015")]

On April 29, 2015, McCutchen recorded his 1,000th career hit, a single off Chicago Cubs' starter [Edwin Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Jackson_(baseball) "Edwin Jackson (baseball)").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-78) On May 24, he was named NL Player of the Week.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Andrew_McCutchen_%2819619033305%29.jpg/250px-Andrew_McCutchen_%2819619033305%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_(19619033305).jpg)

McCutchen in July 2015

In July, McCutchen was selected as an All Star for the fifth consecutive year.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-79) During the game, he hit a solo home run off [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays") pitcher [Chris Archer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Archer "Chris Archer"), joining [Ralph Kiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Kiner "Ralph Kiner"), Willie Stargell, [Roberto Clemente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente "Roberto Clemente"), [Arky Vaughan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arky_Vaughan "Arky Vaughan"), and [Dave Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Parker "Dave Parker") as the sixth Pirate to homer in an All Star Game.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-si.com-80) On August 9, he was again named NL Player of the Week, and in August he was named NL Player of the Month.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

Overall in 2015, McCutchen batted .292/.401 (4th in the National League)/.488 with 23 home runs, nine sacrifice flies (3rd), 98 walks (4th), 12 intentional walks (5th), tied a career-high with 96 RBIs (8th), 12 hit by pitch (9th), 36 doubles (10th), 276 total bases (10th), and 11 stolen bases.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he had two double plays (second among NL center fielders), seven outfield assists (3rd), and a .994 fielding percentage (3rd).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He helped lead the Pirates to a 98-win season (second best in MLB), and their third consecutive Wild Card berth.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-81)

After the season, McCutchen won his fourth straight Silver Slugger.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-si.com-80) He was also named the winner of the 2015 [Roberto Clemente Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente_Award "Roberto Clemente Award"), becoming the first Pirate to win the honor since Willie Stargell in 1974.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-clementeaward-82) He came in 5th in the voting for National League MVP.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Andrew_McCutchen_2016.jpg/250px-Andrew_McCutchen_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_2016.jpg)

McCutchen during spring training 2016

On April 26, 2016, for the second time in his career, McCutchen hit three home runs in a single game against the Colorado Rockies, ending a 3-for-23 slump.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-83)

Overall for the year, McCutchen batted .256 (his lowest-ever batting average)/.336/.430, with 24 home runs and 79 RBIs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) On defense, he was 3rd in the NL in outfield putouts (317), and 5th in center fielder fielding percentage (.991).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

#### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2017")]

During the 2016 [Winter Meetings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Meetings "Winter Meetings"), Pirates' general manager [Neal Huntington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal_Huntington "Neal Huntington") reportedly came close to trading McCutchen to the Washington Nationals.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-84) McCutchen said that he dreaded the possibility of leaving Pittsburgh, and admitted to "googling" his own name in anticipation of a trade.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-85) He later expressed his desire to remain with the Pirates for his entire career.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-86)

In March, McCutchen participated in the [2017 World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Baseball_Classic "2017 World Baseball Classic") with the [United States national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_baseball_team "United States national baseball team").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-87) In the semi-final game against [Team Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_national_baseball_team "Japan national baseball team"), McCutchen hit a RBI-single in a 2–1 victory for Team USA.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-88) On March 22, Team USA defeated [Team Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico_national_baseball_team "Puerto Rico national baseball team") 8–0, to win the first [World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Baseball_Classic "World Baseball Classic") gold medal for the United States.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-89)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Andrew_McCutchen_at-bat_2017_%2834985040992%29.jpg/330px-Andrew_McCutchen_at-bat_2017_%2834985040992%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_at-bat_2017_(34985040992).jpg)

McCutchen in 2017

In June, after hitting .411 with six home runs and only 12 strikeouts, McCutchen was named National League Player of the Month.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-90) On September 26, he hit his first career [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_(baseball) "Grand slam (baseball)").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-91) On October 1, he was named NL Player of the Week.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

In total with the [2017 Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Pittsburgh_Pirates_season "2017 Pittsburgh Pirates season"), McCutchen batted .279/.363/.486, with 28 home runs, 11 stolen bases, and 88 RBIs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He batted .336 against left-handers[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-92) (8th-best in the NL). Defensively, he made 139 appearances in center field and, for the first time in his career, 13 appearances in [right field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_field "Right field"), and his 9 outfield assists were 4th in the National League.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

Having spent the majority of his career with the Pirates, McCutchen holds numerous [PNC Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNC_Park "PNC Park") records. As of July 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit), he had the most games played (676),[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-93) plate appearances (2,873),[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-94) at bats (2,468),[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-95) hits (751),[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-96) multi-hit games (208),[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-97) singles (478),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-98) doubles (161),[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-99) triples (20),[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-100) home runs (92),[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-101) walk-off home runs (6),[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-102) multi-homer games (7),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-103) RBIs (357),[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-104) runs scored (415),[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-105) sacrifice flies (22),[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-106) walks (345),[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-107) intentional walks (41),[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-108) and strikeouts (471).[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-109) He also shared the park record of eight walk-off hits with [Josh Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Harrison "Josh Harrison").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-110)

As of 2018, McCutchen was 2nd of all Pirates players in career power-speed number (185.6; behind Barry Bonds), 4th in home runs (203; behind Hall of Famers Willie Stargell, Ralph Kiner, and Roberto Clemente), 7th in walks (685), extra base hits (539), and sacrifice flies (47), 9th in doubles (292) and intentional walks (63), and 10th in total bases (2,452) and [hit by pitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_by_pitch "Hit by pitch") (61).[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-112)

McCutchen in the [2018 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Major_League_Baseball_season "2018 Major League Baseball season"): with the [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants") (left) and with the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") (right)

On January 15, 2018, the Pirates traded McCutchen to the [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants"), along with cash considerations, in exchange for [Kyle Crick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Crick "Kyle Crick"), [Bryan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Reynolds_(baseball) "Bryan Reynolds (baseball)"), and $500,000 of international bonus slot money.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-113) On April 7, McCutchen had six hits in a game, going six-for-seven with four RBIs against the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), his final hit being a three-run [walk-off home run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk-off_home_run "Walk-off home run") in the 14th inning.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-114) On May 11, the Giants traveled to PNC Park in Pittsburgh, and McCutchen received a standing ovation from Pirates fans.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-115) Overall with the [2018 Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_San_Francisco_Giants_season "2018 San Francisco Giants season"), McCutchen appeared in 130 games, batting .255 with 15 home runs.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-116) He led the club in runs scored (65), doubles (28, tied with Brandon Crawford), RBI (55), stolen bases (13), walks (73), slugging percentage (.415) and on base plus slugging (.772).[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-117) All of his defensive appearances were in right field.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-118)

### New York Yankees (2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: New York Yankees (2018)")]

On August 31, 2018, the Giants traded McCutchen to the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") in exchange for infielder [Abiatal Avelino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiatal_Avelino "Abiatal Avelino") and pitcher Juan De Paula.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-119) In light of the [Yankees personal appearance policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees_appearance_policy "New York Yankees appearance policy"), McCutchen shaved off his beard.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-120) McCutchen also changed his jersey number from 22, which he had worn his entire career, to 26, due to 22 having been assigned to [Jacoby Ellsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacoby_Ellsbury "Jacoby Ellsbury").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-121)

For the 2018 season, between the two teams, McCutchen batted .255/.368/.424 with 20 home runs (his 20 or more home runs for eight straight seasons was the longest active streak among MLB players), 95 walks (8th in the major leagues), 14 stolen bases, and 65 RBIs. With the Yankees he hit. 253 with five home runs and ten RBIs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-122)

### Philadelphia Phillies (2019–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Philadelphia Phillies (2019–2021)")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Andrew_McCutchen_July_18%2C_2020_%2850128244701%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Andrew_McCutchen_July_18%2C_2020_%2850128244701%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_McCutchen_July_18,_2020_(50128244701)_(cropped).jpg)

McCutchen with the Phillies in 2020

On December 12, 2018, the Philadelphia Phillies signed McCutchen to a three-year contract worth $50 million, with a $15 million club option and a $3 million [buyout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buyout "Buyout") for 2022.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-123) On June 3, 2019, McCutchen suffered a knee injury running the bases against the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-124) On June 4, an [MRI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRI "MRI") revealed McCutchen had a [torn ACL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament_injury "Anterior cruciate ligament injury"), and he was ruled out for the rest of the season.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-125) On June 14, he had [surgery to reconstruct the ACL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament_reconstruction "Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction") in his left knee and to repair a [medial meniscus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medial_meniscus "Medial meniscus").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-126) At the time of his injury, he was batting .256/.378/.457 with 10 home runs and 29 RBIs in 219 at bats, leading the NL with 43 walks, and ranked 3rd with 4.45 pitches per plate appearance and 5th with 45 runs scored.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-127)

During the [pandemic-shortened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_sports#North_America "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports")[2020 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Major_League_Baseball_season "2020 Major League Baseball season"), McCutchen hit .253/.324/.433 with 10 home runs and 34 RBIs in 57 games.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-128) Through 2020, he was 5th among active major leaguers in career triples (48), 8th in career walks (845), and 9th in career runs scored (974).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35)

In 2021, McCutchen batted .222/.334/.444 with 27 home runs and 80 RBIs in 144 games, spending most of the season in right field.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-129)

### Milwaukee Brewers (2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Milwaukee Brewers (2022)")]

On March 16, 2022, McCutchen signed a one-year contract with the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") worth $8.5 million.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-130) McCutchen made his Brewers debut on April 7, and recorded a double to the right field corner off [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") starter [Kyle Hendricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Hendricks "Kyle Hendricks") in his first at-bat.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-131) He was placed on the [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") injury list on May 7.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-133) On September 23, McCutchen notched his 1,000th career RBI, scoring [Rowdy Tellez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowdy_Tellez "Rowdy Tellez") on a fielder's choice off of [Cincinnati Reds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Reds "Cincinnati Reds") starter [Luis Cessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Cessa "Luis Cessa").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-134)

In 2022, McCutchen batted .237/.316/.384 (the lowest slugging percentage of his career) with 17 home runs in 515 at bats.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) For the first time in his career, McCutchen made more starts as a designated hitter than in the field, as he logged 82 DH starts compared to 49 outfield starts.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He had the fastest sprint speed of all major league designated hitters, at 28.9 feet/second.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-135)

### Pittsburgh Pirates (2023–2025)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Pittsburgh Pirates (2023–2025)")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/McCutchen_at_bat_in_2025.jpg/250px-McCutchen_at_bat_in_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McCutchen_at_bat_in_2025.jpg)

McCutchen up to bat against the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") in 2025

On January 20, 2023, McCutchen signed a one-year, $5 million contract to return to the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates "Pittsburgh Pirates").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-136) He made his return to PNC Park at the Pirates' home opener on April 7, 2023, where he received a standing ovation that lasted over a minute prior to his first at bat.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-137) McCutchen recorded his 2,000th career hit on June 11, a single off of [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets") starter [Carlos Carrasco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Carrasco_(baseball) "Carlos Carrasco (baseball)").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-138) On September 6, the Pirates placed McCutchen on the 10–day injured list after suffering a season–ending partial left [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon") tear.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-139) He finished the season with 12 home runs, 43 RBIs, and a .256/.378/.397 slash line.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-140) McCutchen became a full-time designated hitter in 2023, with 97 starts at DH and only 7 in the outfield.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-baseball-reference1-35) He became a free agent following the season.

On December 20, 2023, McCutchen signed a one-year, $5 million contract to stay with Pittsburgh.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-141) He stated that he plans to play at least two more seasons and hopes to retire as a Pirate.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-142) On April 14, 2024, McCutchen hit his 300th home run, a two-run shot off of [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies "Philadelphia Phillies") reliever [Ricardo Pinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Pinto_(baseball) "Ricardo Pinto (baseball)").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-143) In 120 appearances for the Pirates, he slashed .232/.328/.411 with 20 home runs and 50 RBI.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-144)

On December 23, 2024, McCutchen re–signed with the Pirates on a one-year, $5 million contract.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-145) On June 1, 2025, McCutchen hit his fourth home run of the season, tying with [Roberto Clemente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente "Roberto Clemente") in third place on the Pirates franchise home run list with 240 home runs.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-146) On June 8, McCutchen recorded his 2,200th career hit against the [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philadelphia_Phillies_season "2025 Philadelphia Phillies season") when he hit a single to left field off of Phillies pitcher [Cristopher Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristopher_S%C3%A1nchez "Cristopher Sánchez"). He becomes the 190th player in MLB history to reach 2,200 career hits.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-147) On June 10, McCutchen hit his sixth home run of the season, passing Roberto Clemente in third place on the Pirates franchise home run list with 241 home runs.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-148) On July 28, McCutchen hit his tenth home run of the season, becoming the 11th player in Major League history to record at least ten home runs in each of their first 17 seasons. The other ten players are [Hank Aaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Aaron "Hank Aaron"), [Eddie Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Murray "Eddie Murray"), [Carl Yastrzemski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Yastrzemski "Carl Yastrzemski"), [Barry Bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Bonds "Barry Bonds"), [Albert Pujols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Pujols "Albert Pujols"), [Frank Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Robinson "Frank Robinson"), [Harold Baines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Baines "Harold Baines"), [Mickey Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mantle "Mickey Mantle"), [Jeff Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Kent "Jeff Kent"), and [Willie McCovey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_McCovey "Willie McCovey").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-149) In 135 appearances for the Pirates, he slashed .239/.333/.367 with 13 home runs and 57 RBI.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-150)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_McCutchen&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Wolf_McCutchen_Harper_%2832686597377%29.jpg/250px-Wolf_McCutchen_Harper_%2832686597377%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wolf_McCutchen_Harper_(32686597377).jpg)

McCutchen with Governor [Tom Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Wolf "Tom Wolf") and Phillies teammate [Bryce Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Harper "Bryce Harper") in 2019

Early in his career, McCutchen was known across the league for his long [dreadlocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreadlocks "Dreadlocks").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-nbc-8)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-162) Before the 2014 MLB season, he told the _[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh\_Tribune-Review "Pittsburgh Tribune-Review")_: "It's good to have an image. I have the hair, but eventually I'm gonna cut it".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-trib-64) On March 25, 2015, McCutchen cut his dreadlocks, which were sold through MLB's website via auction, with all proceeds benefiting Pirates Charities.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-163) McCutchen teased his fans on [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media") for a big "secret" before unveiling his new haircut.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-164)

McCutchen is active on [X (Formerly Twitter)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") and [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), often posting and engaging with fans.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-165) In 2020, McCutchen spawned his alter ego, "Uncle Larry," after Fox Philadelphia sports anchor [Howard Eskin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Eskin "Howard Eskin") confused McCutchen for 1970s [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") running back [Lawrence McCutcheon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_McCutcheon "Lawrence McCutcheon").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-166) McCutchen appeared as Uncle Larry during a May 2020 episode of MLB Network's Intentional Talk, sporting sunglasses, a wig, and a half-unbuttoned jersey.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-168) The Uncle Larry gig spawned a rash of merchandise, including t-shirts, a bobblehead, and a trading card in 2021.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-169)

McCutchen proposed to his longtime girlfriend Maria Hanslovan on the December 11, 2013, episode of _[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ellen\_DeGeneres\_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")_.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-170) On November 27, 2017, McCutchen and his wife announced the birth of their first child, a son.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-171) On December 24, 2019, McCutchen and his wife announced the birth of their second son, and on October 25, 2021, it was announced on Instagram that Maria gave birth to their first daughter.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-172) On March 9, 2024, a second daughter was born.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-k529-173) They reside in [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-174)

McCutchen, the son of a minister, is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-175)

In May 2021, McCutchen provided [voice acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_acting "Voice acting") for an episode of the [Disney Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Junior "Disney Junior") television show _[Puppy Dog Pals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puppy\_Dog\_Pals "Puppy Dog Pals")_. He voiced "a cool, card-playing dog" who helps the main characters find an autographed [baseball card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_card "Baseball card") of their favorite player, voiced by [Mookie Betts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookie_Betts "Mookie Betts").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_McCutchen#cite_note-176)

**Yasiel Puig Valdés** ([/ˈ j ɑː s i ɛ l ˈ p w iː ɡ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_YAH-see-el PWEEG_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), Catalan name: Puig (meaning Hill); born December 7, 1990) is a Cuban-born American professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball")[right fielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_fielder "Right fielder") for the [Toronto Maple Leafs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Maple_Leafs_(Canadian_Baseball_League) "Toronto Maple Leafs (Canadian Baseball League)") of the [Canadian Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Baseball_League "Canadian Baseball League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-1) He played in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB) for the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), [Cincinnati Reds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Reds "Cincinnati Reds"), and [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians"), and in the [KBO League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBO_League "KBO League") for the [Kiwoom Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiwoom_Heroes "Kiwoom Heroes"). He also played in Mexico, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, and Cuba. His nickname was "the Wild Horse", given to him by longtime Dodgers broadcaster [Vin Scully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_Scully "Vin Scully").

Puig played for the [Cuba national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_national_baseball_team "Cuba national baseball team") in the [2008 World Junior Baseball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Junior_Baseball_Championship "2008 World Junior Baseball Championship"), winning a [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal"). He [defected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_baseball_players_who_defected_from_Cuba "List of baseball players who defected from Cuba") from Cuba in 2012 and signed a seven-year, $42 million contract with the Dodgers. He made his MLB debut on June 3, 2013. That season, Puig hit .319 in 104 games with 19 home runs, and was selected by _Baseball America_ to their annual "All-Rookie team". The following season, he started in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"). The Dodgers traded Puig to the Reds before the 2019 season, and the Reds traded Puig to the Indians at the 2019 [trade deadline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_(sports)#MLB_2 "Trade (sports)").

Puig did not sign with a team in 2020, and played for [El Águila de Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_%C3%81guila_de_Veracruz "El Águila de Veracruz") of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League "Mexican Baseball League") in 2021. He signed with the Heroes for the 2022 season. He played for Veracruz again in 2024 and the Heroes in 2025.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Yasiel Puig Valdés was born on December 7, 1990, in [Cienfuegos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cienfuegos "Cienfuegos"), Cuba, the elder of two children of Omar Puig and Maritza Valdés. He has a sister, Yaima. His father was an engineer in a [sugar cane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_cane "Sugar cane") factory. He began playing baseball at the age of nine.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-2)

## Cuban career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cuban career")]

Puig played for the [Cuba national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_national_baseball_team "Cuba national baseball team") when they won the [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") in the [2008 World Junior Baseball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Junior_Baseball_Championship "2008 World Junior Baseball Championship"). He then played for the [Cienfuegos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cienfuegos_(baseball) "Cienfuegos (baseball)") team of the [Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_National_Series "Cuban National Series") in the [2008–09 Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Cuban_National_Series "2008–09 Cuban National Series"). He [batted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") .276 with five [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") in his debut season. Puig enjoyed a breakout season in the [2009–10 Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cuban_National_Series "2009–10 Cuban National Series"), with a .330 batting average, 17 home runs, 47 [runs batted in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_batted_in "Runs batted in") (RBIs), and 78 [runs scored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_scored "Runs scored") in 327 [at-bats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-bats "At-bats").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb.com-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-4) Puig also played for Cuba in the [2011 World Port Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Port_Tournament "2011 World Port Tournament"), where he tried to defect along with teammate [Gerardo Concepción](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerardo_Concepci%C3%B3n "Gerardo Concepción"). Concepción was successful, but Puig was not and was then banned from playing the 2011–12 seasons.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:3-5)

## Defection from Cuba to Mexico

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Defection from Cuba to Mexico")]

Starting in 2009, Puig tried to defect to [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") 13 times in order to become a legal resident so he could become eligible to sign a contract in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb.com-3) The first time, police pulled over Puig's car. The second time, the boat failed to arrive. The third time, police raided their safe house and detained them for six days. On the fourth try, the [U.S. Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Coast_Guard "U.S. Coast Guard")[Cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Coast_Guard_Cutter "U.S. Coast Guard Cutter")[_Vigilant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Vigilant_(WMEC-617) "USCGC Vigilant (WMEC-617)") intercepted their boat near [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"). The fifth time, he was successfully taken to Mexico by the [Los Zetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Zetas "Los Zetas") drug cartel. Yunior Despaigne, a boxer who was formerly on the Cuba national team and had known Puig for years through youth sports academies, said he "[didn't] know if you could call it a kidnapping, because we had gone there voluntarily, but we also weren't free to leave." He added that the cartel threatened to "give him a _machetazo_" (a whack with a machete) if the payment failed to go through.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:6-6)

Floridian Raul Pacheco, the 29-year-old president of Miami-based T&P Metal and PY Recycling, allegedly paid smugglers $250,000 to get Puig out of Cuba. In exchange, Pacheco would receive 20% of Puig's future earnings after he signed an MLB contract. Pacheco had previously been arrested in 2009 for attempted [burglary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burglary "Burglary") and in 2010 for using a fake [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America") credit card to buy $150,000 worth of beer and having in his possession four other fraudulent credit cards and a [fake ID card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_identification "Fake identification"). He was sentenced to two years’ probation. According to court records, Puig has paid Pacheco over $1.3 million. He also paid $400,000 to $500,000 to Alberto Fariñas, the 49-year-old vice president of Pacheco's T&P Metal company, and $600,000 to Marcos González, a Miami lawyer. He also paid an undisclosed amount to Gilberto Suarez, founder of a start-up company called Miami Sport Management. A month after Puig left Cuba, the captain of the smuggling boat, Yandrys León, described as "one of the most important capos of the [Cuban-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban-American "Cuban-American")[mafia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mafia_in_the_United_States "Mafia in the United States")", was found dead in [Cancún](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canc%C3%BAn "Cancún").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:1-7)

[Cuban boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_in_Cuba "Boxing in Cuba") Miguel Angel Corbacho Daudinot was sentenced to seven years in prison after Puig allegedly testified against him to the Cuban authorities. In 2013, Corbacho Daudinot's lawyers filed a federal lawsuit against Puig in Miami, claiming Puig delivered false testimony that led to Corbacho Daudinot's imprisonment under "inhumane" conditions, and in so doing violated the [Torture Victim Protection Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture_Victim_Protection_Act "Torture Victim Protection Act"); the suit sought $12 million in damages.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:6-6)

Puig had been offered to Los Angeles-based agent Gus Dominguez, starting at $175,000, and New York-based agent [Joe Kehoskie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kehoskie "Joe Kehoskie"), starting at $250,000, the latter of whom said that "nobody's going to Cuba [...] and just handing him over to an agent out of the goodness of their heart."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:1-7)
