### Los Angeles Dodgers (2013–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Los Angeles Dodgers (2013–2018)")]

#### Minor leagues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Minor leagues")]

The [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers") signed Puig on June 28, 2012, to a seven-year contract worth $42 million.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb-8)[Eddie Oropesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Oropesa "Eddie Oropesa") and Tim Bravo, a special-education teacher from [Las Cruces High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces_High_School "Las Cruces High School") in New Mexico, helped the newly arrived Puig adjust to life in the United States during his first year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-know-9)

The Dodgers placed Puig on the 40-man roster and assigned him to their [Arizona Rookie League team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_League_Dodgers "Arizona League Dodgers"). In nine games, he hit .400 with four homers and 11 RBI. On August 13, the Dodgers promoted Puig to the [Rancho Cucamonga Quakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga_Quakes "Rancho Cucamonga Quakes") of the [Class A-Advanced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_A-Advanced "Class A-Advanced")[California League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_League "California League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-10) He played in 14 games with the Quakes and hit .327. After the Quakes season, he was scheduled to join the [Mesa Solar Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_Solar_Sox "Mesa Solar Sox") of the [Arizona Fall League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Fall_League "Arizona Fall League"), but a [staph infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staph_infection "Staph infection") in his right elbow required surgery and sidelined him for several months. After the infection healed, he opted to play [winter ball in Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_de_B%C3%A9isbol_Profesional_Roberto_Clemente "Liga de Béisbol Profesional Roberto Clemente") to keep his development on schedule.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-11)

Puig had a strong [spring training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_training "Spring training") with the Dodgers in 2013, hitting .526 in [Cactus League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus_League "Cactus League") games and having some in the press speculate that he might break camp with the Dodgers. However, he was optioned to the [Double-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-A_(baseball) "Double-A (baseball)")[Chattanooga Lookouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chattanooga_Lookouts "Chattanooga Lookouts") just before the end of spring training.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-12) He hit .313 with eight home runs and 37 RBI for the Lookouts in 40 games.

#### 2013

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2013")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Yasiel_Puig.JPG/250px-Yasiel_Puig.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yasiel_Puig.JPG)

Puig at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") for the [2013 Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "2013 Los Angeles Dodgers season")

On June 2, 2013, the Dodgers announced they had recalled Puig from Double-A.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-13) He made his MLB debut on June 3. In his first at bat, he singled to left-center off [Eric Stults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stults "Eric Stults") of the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_San_Diego_Padres_season "2013 San Diego Padres season"). He went 2-for-4 and showed his strong arm by recording an outfield assist on a double play to end the game.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-14)

Puig hit two home runs, doubled, and drove in five runs in his second game. He became the first Dodger ever to have a multi-homer game in one of his first two appearances.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-15) In his fourth game, on June 6, he hit a [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_(baseball) "Grand slam (baseball)") off [Cory Gearrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Gearrin "Cory Gearrin") of the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Atlanta_Braves_season "2013 Atlanta Braves season").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-16) Puig was named the [National League Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") for the week of June 3–9.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-17)

Puig had 27 hits in his first 15 games, tied with [Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio") ([1936](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_New_York_Yankees_season "1936 New York Yankees season")) and [Terry Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Pendleton "Terry Pendleton") ([1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "1984 St. Louis Cardinals season")) for second-most all-time behind [Irv Waldron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irv_Waldron "Irv Waldron") ([1901](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1901_Milwaukee_Brewers_season "1901 Milwaukee Brewers season")) and [Bo Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Hart "Bo Hart") ([2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "2003 St. Louis Cardinals season")) with 28.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-19) Puig also became the first player in major league history to record at least 34 hits and seven home runs in his first 20 games and set Dodger records for most hits through 20 games (one more than [Gibby Brack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibby_Brack "Gibby Brack") in [1937](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1937_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1937 Brooklyn Dodgers season")) and total bases through 20 games (58, four more than [Del Bissonette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Bissonette "Del Bissonette") in [1928](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Brooklyn_Robins_season "1928 Brooklyn Robins season")).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-20) Puig finished June with 44 hits, breaking [Steve Sax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Sax "Steve Sax")'s [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "1983 Los Angeles Dodgers season") team record for most hits by a rookie in one month. That total was also second all-time for rookies in their first month, behind only DiMaggio who had 48.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-21) In 26 games in June, Puig hit .436 with a .467 on-base percentage and a .713 slugging percentage. He won both the [National League Rookie of the Month Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Rookie_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Rookie of the Month Award") and the [National League Player of the Month Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award"), the first time someone had won both in their first month in the majors.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-22)

Despite his not making his debut until June, Puig received 842,915 fan write-in votes for the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2013 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"). His name was included among the [All-Star Final Vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Final_Vote "All-Star Final Vote") candidates.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-23) In that vote, Puig finished second to [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") first baseman [Freddie Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Freeman "Freddie Freeman").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-25)

Puig cooled in September, batting .214 in the final month of the season.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:4-26) In 2013, Puig hit .319 in 104 games with 19 home runs and 42 RBIs. He was selected by _[Baseball America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball\_America "Baseball America")_ to their annual "All-Rookie team"[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-27) and finished second in the [National League Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_League_Rookie_of_the_Year "National League Rookie of the Year") voting to fellow Cuban [José Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Fern%C3%A1ndez_(right-handed_pitcher) "José Fernández (right-handed pitcher)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-28) Puig hit well in his first postseason, hitting .333 in 10 games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:5-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-30) However, he grounded into a double play in the 9th inning of the team's Game 4 loss in the [National League Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_National_League_Championship_Series "2013 National League Championship Series") (NLCS).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:4-26)

#### 2014

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_%283%29.JPG/250px-20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_%283%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_(3).JPG)

Puig's following a swing for the [2014 Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "2014 Los Angeles Dodgers season")

On May 17, 2014, Puig had his eighth consecutive game with at least one extra-base hit and at least one RBI, which was a new record for the longest streak by a Dodger, surpassing [Pedro Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Guerrero_(baseball,_born_1956) "Pedro Guerrero (baseball, born 1956)") ([1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "1985 Los Angeles Dodgers season")), [Duke Snider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Snider "Duke Snider") ([1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1954 Brooklyn Dodgers season")), and [Howie Schultz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howie_Schultz "Howie Schultz") ([1944](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1944 Brooklyn Dodgers season")).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-31) He was selected as the NL Player of the Week for that week[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-32) and the NL Player of the Month for May after he hit .398 with eight home runs and 25 RBI.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-33) Puig was voted and named a starter for the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), the youngest Dodger starter for an All-Star game since [Steve Sax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Sax "Steve Sax") in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "1982 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-34) Puig also participated in the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_Home_Run_Derby "2014 Major League Baseball Home Run Derby").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-35)

On July 25, Puig went 4-for-5 with a career-high four extra-base hits, tying the Dodgers' single-game record with three triples, matching [Jimmy Sheckard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Sheckard "Jimmy Sheckard").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-espn-36) Puig's teammates [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp") and [Dee Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Gordon "Dee Gordon") each recorded one triple as well, tying the club's single-game triples record of five, set in 1902 and 1921.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-37)

Puig finished the [2014 regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_season "2014 Major League Baseball season") with 16 home runs and 69 RBI, and a .296 batting average. In the [National League Division Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_National_League_Division_Series "2014 National League Division Series") (NLDS) against the [St. Louis Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "2014 St. Louis Cardinals season"), Puig struck out seven times in a row over the first three games of the series. He then hit a triple and scored the Dodgers' only run in a 3–1 loss.

Puig was selected to travel to Japan after the season for the [2014 MLB Japan All-Star Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_MLB_Japan_All-Star_Series "2014 MLB Japan All-Star Series"), playing against All-Stars of [Nippon Professional Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nippon_Professional_Baseball "Nippon Professional Baseball").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-38)

Puig began the 2015 season experiencing left hamstring issues that caused him to miss several games. On April 26, Puig was placed on the 15-day [disabled list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_list "Disabled list") for the first time in his major league career, due to his nagging left hamstring.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-40) He rejoined the Dodgers roster on June 6.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-41) On August 18, Puig injured his right hamstring, and he was placed on the 15-day disabled list nine days later.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-42) He returned on October 3, appearing in the final two games of the season. On February 7, 2018, [Wasserman Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasserman_Media_Group "Wasserman Media Group") announced that it had "terminated its professional relationship" with Puig.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-52) He was without representation until April, when he signed with Beverly Hills Sports Council.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-53) On April 28, Puig left a game due to left hip soreness. He was placed on the 10-day disabled list the next day.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-54) On August 11, Puig hit his 100th career home run off [Kyle Freeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Freeland "Kyle Freeland") of the [Colorado Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies "Colorado Rockies"). On August 14, Puig got into an altercation with [Nick Hundley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Hundley "Nick Hundley") at home plate. After fouling off a pitch, Puig threw his bat up and snatched it out of the air in frustration feeling like he had a good pitch to hit. Hundley took exception to Puig's actions and the two had words. Puig then shoved Hundley, causing a bench-clearing brawl. Both Hundley and Puig were ejected.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-55) In 2018, Puig had the lowest fielding percentage among all major league outfielders.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-56) Throughout the season, he struggled against left-handed pitching.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-57)

In Game 7 of the [NLCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_National_League_Championship_Series "2018 National League Championship Series"), Puig hit a three-run home run to extend the Dodger lead to 5–1 against the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") in a game they would win for their second consecutive [pennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_National_League_pennant_winners "List of National League pennant winners"). ### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

In April 2013, Puig was charged with [reckless driving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reckless_driving "Reckless driving") and [speeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speeding "Speeding") in [Chattanooga, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chattanooga,_Tennessee "Chattanooga, Tennessee"), after allegedly driving 97 miles per hour (156 km/h) in a 50 mph (80 km/h) zone on Amnicola Highway.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-82) The charges were dismissed after he served 12 hours of [community service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_service "Community service").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-cbssports1-83) On December 28, 2013, Puig was again arrested for reckless driving after allegedly driving 110 mph (180 km/h) in a 70 mph (110 km/h) zone, in [Naples, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples,_Florida "Naples, Florida"). He was taken to the [Collier County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collier_County,_Florida "Collier County, Florida") Jail[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-cbssports1-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-84) and released after posting [bail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bail "Bail"). Prosecutors elected to drop the reckless driving charge on January 28, 2014, after concluding that there was insufficient evidence to support it.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-85)

In March 2021, [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") reported that MLB investigators had interviewed a woman who said Puig had sexually assaulted her in a [Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") bathroom during a [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") game in October 2018. Puig has denied the allegations, calling them "false and malicious". The woman did not file a police report but later filed a lawsuit.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-CloudFuture-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-87) In October 2021, Puig announced that he had settled his sexual assault lawsuit and wished to return to MLB in 2022.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-88)

In December 2021, _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ reported that Puig had secretly settled a lawsuit filed by two women who claimed that Puig sexually assaulted them in January 2017. Despite the allegations, Puig had not been put on leave, and the lawsuit was not publicized. As part of the disclosure from the 2020 lawsuit, Puig's attorneys claimed that Puig was insolvent and that his earlier career earnings were nearly exhausted. The latest settlement was for $250,000, with the accuser paying her own attorney's fees, due to fears that Puig had nothing left to offer had the accuser held out for more.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-90)

In November 2022, Puig agreed to plead guilty to lying to federal law enforcement officers regarding bets that he placed with an illegal [sports betting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_betting "Sports betting") operation. He faced up to five years in prison.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-92) Later that month, he changed his plea to not guilty.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-f692-93) In 2025, a federal appeals court agreed with a trial court ruling that Puig's plea deal had not been accepted by a court. He still faced a jury trial regarding the illegal bets, from which he allegedly incurred $282,900 in gambling debts.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-94)

On February 6, 2026, Puig was found guilty of two federal charges: [making false statements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_false_statements "Making false statements") to investigators and [obstructing justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstruction_of_justice_in_the_United_States "Obstruction of justice in the United States").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-95) The guilty findings could result in up to 20 years imprisonment; sentencing was set for May 26, 2026, but was later pushed back to June 30, 2026, following a post-trial acquittal motion from Puig.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-97) On June 26, 2026, Judge [Dolly M. Gee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Gee "Dolly Gee") agreed to a request from Puig to postpone his sentencing from June 30, 2026, to July 28, 2026, to give him more time to report his finances to the court.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-98)

### Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

[![Image 14: Yasiel Puig, facing away, wearing a black Cleveland uniform with "Wild Horse" written on the back.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Puig_Wild_Horse_%2848663858233%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Puig_Wild_Horse_%2848663858233%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Puig_Wild_Horse_(48663858233)_(cropped).jpg)

Puig wearing a "Wild Horse" jersey in 2019.

Puig created the Wild Horse Children's Foundation in 2016. The foundation's name embraces the nickname [Vin Scully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_Scully "Vin Scully") gave him in 2013.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-99)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:2-80) According to its website, the foundation aimed to inspire children and families in underserved communities by promoting healthier and better-quality lives through education, sports, community development, and health and wellness programs.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-100)

On April 19, 2018, Puig and the Wild Horse Children's Foundation announced a collaboration with the City of [San Fernando, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando,_California "San Fernando, California") to renovate Pioneer Park and refurbish a dilapidated house on-site that had been boarded up for nearly 10 years.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-101)

At a game in New York in May 2019, Puig met a young fan about to have his 40th surgery, due to [hydrocephalus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocephalus "Hydrocephalus").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-102) The following month, Puig treated the fan and his family to a Reds game in Cincinnati.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-103)

On an off-day in New York between two Indians' series (one with the [Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets") and one with the [Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees")) in August 2019, Puig paid for a helicopter trip to Camp Simcha, an orthodox Jewish day camp for kids with cancer. He spent four hours with the children there and found it difficult to leave. In a tweet afterward, Puig called it "one of the best days of my life", adding, "you are my inspiration".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-104)

**Yasiel Puig Valdés** ([/ˈ j ɑː s i ɛ l ˈ p w iː ɡ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_YAH-see-el PWEEG_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), Catalan name: Puig (meaning Hill); born December 7, 1990) is a Cuban-born American professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball")[right fielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_fielder "Right fielder") for the [Toronto Maple Leafs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Maple_Leafs_(Canadian_Baseball_League) "Toronto Maple Leafs (Canadian Baseball League)") of the [Canadian Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Baseball_League "Canadian Baseball League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-1) He played in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB) for the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), [Cincinnati Reds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Reds "Cincinnati Reds"), and [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians"), and in the [KBO League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBO_League "KBO League") for the [Kiwoom Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiwoom_Heroes "Kiwoom Heroes"). He also played in Mexico, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, and Cuba. His nickname was "the Wild Horse", given to him by longtime Dodgers broadcaster [Vin Scully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_Scully "Vin Scully").

Puig played for the [Cuba national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_national_baseball_team "Cuba national baseball team") in the [2008 World Junior Baseball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Junior_Baseball_Championship "2008 World Junior Baseball Championship"), winning a [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal"). He [defected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_baseball_players_who_defected_from_Cuba "List of baseball players who defected from Cuba") from Cuba in 2012 and signed a seven-year, $42 million contract with the Dodgers. He made his MLB debut on June 3, 2013. That season, Puig hit .319 in 104 games with 19 home runs, and was selected by _Baseball America_ to their annual "All-Rookie team". The following season, he started in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"). The Dodgers traded Puig to the Reds before the 2019 season, and the Reds traded Puig to the Indians at the 2019 [trade deadline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_(sports)#MLB_2 "Trade (sports)").

Puig did not sign with a team in 2020, and played for [El Águila de Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_%C3%81guila_de_Veracruz "El Águila de Veracruz") of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League "Mexican Baseball League") in 2021. He signed with the Heroes for the 2022 season. He played for Veracruz again in 2024 and the Heroes in 2025.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Yasiel Puig Valdés was born on December 7, 1990, in [Cienfuegos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cienfuegos "Cienfuegos"), Cuba, the elder of two children of Omar Puig and Maritza Valdés. He has a sister, Yaima. His father was an engineer in a [sugar cane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_cane "Sugar cane") factory. He began playing baseball at the age of nine.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-2)

## Cuban career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cuban career")]

Puig played for the [Cuba national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_national_baseball_team "Cuba national baseball team") when they won the [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") in the [2008 World Junior Baseball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Junior_Baseball_Championship "2008 World Junior Baseball Championship"). He then played for the [Cienfuegos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cienfuegos_(baseball) "Cienfuegos (baseball)") team of the [Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_National_Series "Cuban National Series") in the [2008–09 Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Cuban_National_Series "2008–09 Cuban National Series"). He [batted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball) "Batting average (baseball)") .276 with five [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") in his debut season. Puig enjoyed a breakout season in the [2009–10 Cuban National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cuban_National_Series "2009–10 Cuban National Series"), with a .330 batting average, 17 home runs, 47 [runs batted in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_batted_in "Runs batted in") (RBIs), and 78 [runs scored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_scored "Runs scored") in 327 [at-bats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-bats "At-bats").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb.com-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-4) Puig also played for Cuba in the [2011 World Port Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Port_Tournament "2011 World Port Tournament"), where he tried to defect along with teammate [Gerardo Concepción](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerardo_Concepci%C3%B3n "Gerardo Concepción"). Concepción was successful, but Puig was not and was then banned from playing the 2011–12 seasons.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:3-5)

## Defection from Cuba to Mexico

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Defection from Cuba to Mexico")]

Starting in 2009, Puig tried to defect to [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") 13 times in order to become a legal resident so he could become eligible to sign a contract in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb.com-3) The first time, police pulled over Puig's car. The second time, the boat failed to arrive. The third time, police raided their safe house and detained them for six days. On the fourth try, the [U.S. Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Coast_Guard "U.S. Coast Guard")[Cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Coast_Guard_Cutter "U.S. Coast Guard Cutter")[_Vigilant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Vigilant_(WMEC-617) "USCGC Vigilant (WMEC-617)") intercepted their boat near [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"). The fifth time, he was successfully taken to Mexico by the [Los Zetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Zetas "Los Zetas") drug cartel. Yunior Despaigne, a boxer who was formerly on the Cuba national team and had known Puig for years through youth sports academies, said he "[didn't] know if you could call it a kidnapping, because we had gone there voluntarily, but we also weren't free to leave." He added that the cartel threatened to "give him a _machetazo_" (a whack with a machete) if the payment failed to go through.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:6-6)

Floridian Raul Pacheco, the 29-year-old president of Miami-based T&P Metal and PY Recycling, allegedly paid smugglers $250,000 to get Puig out of Cuba. In exchange, Pacheco would receive 20% of Puig's future earnings after he signed an MLB contract. Pacheco had previously been arrested in 2009 for attempted [burglary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burglary "Burglary") and in 2010 for using a fake [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America") credit card to buy $150,000 worth of beer and having in his possession four other fraudulent credit cards and a [fake ID card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_identification "Fake identification"). He was sentenced to two years’ probation. According to court records, Puig has paid Pacheco over $1.3 million. He also paid $400,000 to $500,000 to Alberto Fariñas, the 49-year-old vice president of Pacheco's T&P Metal company, and $600,000 to Marcos González, a Miami lawyer. He also paid an undisclosed amount to Gilberto Suarez, founder of a start-up company called Miami Sport Management. A month after Puig left Cuba, the captain of the smuggling boat, Yandrys León, described as "one of the most important capos of the [Cuban-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban-American "Cuban-American")[mafia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mafia_in_the_United_States "Mafia in the United States")", was found dead in [Cancún](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canc%C3%BAn "Cancún").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:1-7)

[Cuban boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_in_Cuba "Boxing in Cuba") Miguel Angel Corbacho Daudinot was sentenced to seven years in prison after Puig allegedly testified against him to the Cuban authorities. In 2013, Corbacho Daudinot's lawyers filed a federal lawsuit against Puig in Miami, claiming Puig delivered false testimony that led to Corbacho Daudinot's imprisonment under "inhumane" conditions, and in so doing violated the [Torture Victim Protection Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture_Victim_Protection_Act "Torture Victim Protection Act"); the suit sought $12 million in damages.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:6-6)

Puig had been offered to Los Angeles-based agent Gus Dominguez, starting at $175,000, and New York-based agent [Joe Kehoskie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kehoskie "Joe Kehoskie"), starting at $250,000, the latter of whom said that "nobody's going to Cuba [...] and just handing him over to an agent out of the goodness of their heart."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:1-7)

### Los Angeles Dodgers (2013–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Los Angeles Dodgers (2013–2018)")]

#### Minor leagues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Minor leagues")]

The [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers") signed Puig on June 28, 2012, to a seven-year contract worth $42 million.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-mlb-8)[Eddie Oropesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Oropesa "Eddie Oropesa") and Tim Bravo, a special-education teacher from [Las Cruces High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces_High_School "Las Cruces High School") in New Mexico, helped the newly arrived Puig adjust to life in the United States during his first year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-know-9)

The Dodgers placed Puig on the 40-man roster and assigned him to their [Arizona Rookie League team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_League_Dodgers "Arizona League Dodgers"). In nine games, he hit .400 with four homers and 11 RBI. On August 13, the Dodgers promoted Puig to the [Rancho Cucamonga Quakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga_Quakes "Rancho Cucamonga Quakes") of the [Class A-Advanced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_A-Advanced "Class A-Advanced")[California League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_League "California League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-10) He played in 14 games with the Quakes and hit .327. After the Quakes season, he was scheduled to join the [Mesa Solar Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_Solar_Sox "Mesa Solar Sox") of the [Arizona Fall League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Fall_League "Arizona Fall League"), but a [staph infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staph_infection "Staph infection") in his right elbow required surgery and sidelined him for several months. After the infection healed, he opted to play [winter ball in Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_de_B%C3%A9isbol_Profesional_Roberto_Clemente "Liga de Béisbol Profesional Roberto Clemente") to keep his development on schedule.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-11)

Puig had a strong [spring training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_training "Spring training") with the Dodgers in 2013, hitting .526 in [Cactus League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus_League "Cactus League") games and having some in the press speculate that he might break camp with the Dodgers. However, he was optioned to the [Double-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-A_(baseball) "Double-A (baseball)")[Chattanooga Lookouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chattanooga_Lookouts "Chattanooga Lookouts") just before the end of spring training.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-12) He hit .313 with eight home runs and 37 RBI for the Lookouts in 40 games.

#### 2013

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2013")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Yasiel_Puig.JPG/250px-Yasiel_Puig.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yasiel_Puig.JPG)

Puig at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") for the [2013 Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "2013 Los Angeles Dodgers season")

On June 2, 2013, the Dodgers announced they had recalled Puig from Double-A.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-13) He made his MLB debut on June 3. In his first at bat, he singled to left-center off [Eric Stults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stults "Eric Stults") of the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_San_Diego_Padres_season "2013 San Diego Padres season"). He went 2-for-4 and showed his strong arm by recording an outfield assist on a double play to end the game.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-14)

Puig hit two home runs, doubled, and drove in five runs in his second game. He became the first Dodger ever to have a multi-homer game in one of his first two appearances.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-15) In his fourth game, on June 6, he hit a [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_(baseball) "Grand slam (baseball)") off [Cory Gearrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Gearrin "Cory Gearrin") of the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Atlanta_Braves_season "2013 Atlanta Braves season").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-16) Puig was named the [National League Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") for the week of June 3–9.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-17)

Puig had 27 hits in his first 15 games, tied with [Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio") ([1936](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_New_York_Yankees_season "1936 New York Yankees season")) and [Terry Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Pendleton "Terry Pendleton") ([1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "1984 St. Louis Cardinals season")) for second-most all-time behind [Irv Waldron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irv_Waldron "Irv Waldron") ([1901](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1901_Milwaukee_Brewers_season "1901 Milwaukee Brewers season")) and [Bo Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Hart "Bo Hart") ([2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "2003 St. Louis Cardinals season")) with 28.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-19) Puig also became the first player in major league history to record at least 34 hits and seven home runs in his first 20 games and set Dodger records for most hits through 20 games (one more than [Gibby Brack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibby_Brack "Gibby Brack") in [1937](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1937_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1937 Brooklyn Dodgers season")) and total bases through 20 games (58, four more than [Del Bissonette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Bissonette "Del Bissonette") in [1928](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Brooklyn_Robins_season "1928 Brooklyn Robins season")).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-20) Puig finished June with 44 hits, breaking [Steve Sax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Sax "Steve Sax")'s [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "1983 Los Angeles Dodgers season") team record for most hits by a rookie in one month. That total was also second all-time for rookies in their first month, behind only DiMaggio who had 48.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-21) In 26 games in June, Puig hit .436 with a .467 on-base percentage and a .713 slugging percentage. He won both the [National League Rookie of the Month Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Rookie_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Rookie of the Month Award") and the [National League Player of the Month Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award"), the first time someone had won both in their first month in the majors.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-22)

Despite his not making his debut until June, Puig received 842,915 fan write-in votes for the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2013 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"). His name was included among the [All-Star Final Vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Final_Vote "All-Star Final Vote") candidates.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-23) In that vote, Puig finished second to [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves") first baseman [Freddie Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Freeman "Freddie Freeman").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-25)

Puig cooled in September, batting .214 in the final month of the season.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:4-26) In 2013, Puig hit .319 in 104 games with 19 home runs and 42 RBIs. He was selected by _[Baseball America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball\_America "Baseball America")_ to their annual "All-Rookie team"[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-27) and finished second in the [National League Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_League_Rookie_of_the_Year "National League Rookie of the Year") voting to fellow Cuban [José Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Fern%C3%A1ndez_(right-handed_pitcher) "José Fernández (right-handed pitcher)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-28) Puig hit well in his first postseason, hitting .333 in 10 games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:5-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-30) However, he grounded into a double play in the 9th inning of the team's Game 4 loss in the [National League Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_National_League_Championship_Series "2013 National League Championship Series") (NLCS).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:4-26)

#### 2014

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_%283%29.JPG/250px-20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_%283%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20140919_Yasiel_Puig_at_bat_(3).JPG)

Puig's following a swing for the [2014 Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "2014 Los Angeles Dodgers season")

On May 17, 2014, Puig had his eighth consecutive game with at least one extra-base hit and at least one RBI, which was a new record for the longest streak by a Dodger, surpassing [Pedro Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Guerrero_(baseball,_born_1956) "Pedro Guerrero (baseball, born 1956)") ([1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "1985 Los Angeles Dodgers season")), [Duke Snider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Snider "Duke Snider") ([1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1954 Brooklyn Dodgers season")), and [Howie Schultz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howie_Schultz "Howie Schultz") ([1944](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1944 Brooklyn Dodgers season")).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-31) He was selected as the NL Player of the Week for that week[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-32) and the NL Player of the Month for May after he hit .398 with eight home runs and 25 RBI.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-33) Puig was voted and named a starter for the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2014 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), the youngest Dodger starter for an All-Star game since [Steve Sax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Sax "Steve Sax") in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "1982 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-34) Puig also participated in the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_Home_Run_Derby "2014 Major League Baseball Home Run Derby").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-35)

On July 25, Puig went 4-for-5 with a career-high four extra-base hits, tying the Dodgers' single-game record with three triples, matching [Jimmy Sheckard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Sheckard "Jimmy Sheckard").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-espn-36) Puig's teammates [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp") and [Dee Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Gordon "Dee Gordon") each recorded one triple as well, tying the club's single-game triples record of five, set in 1902 and 1921.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-37)

Puig finished the [2014 regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_season "2014 Major League Baseball season") with 16 home runs and 69 RBI, and a .296 batting average. In the [National League Division Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_National_League_Division_Series "2014 National League Division Series") (NLDS) against the [St. Louis Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_St._Louis_Cardinals_season "2014 St. Louis Cardinals season"), Puig struck out seven times in a row over the first three games of the series. He then hit a triple and scored the Dodgers' only run in a 3–1 loss.

Puig was selected to travel to Japan after the season for the [2014 MLB Japan All-Star Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_MLB_Japan_All-Star_Series "2014 MLB Japan All-Star Series"), playing against All-Stars of [Nippon Professional Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nippon_Professional_Baseball "Nippon Professional Baseball").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-38)

#### 2015

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2015")]

Puig began the 2015 season experiencing left hamstring issues that caused him to miss several games. On April 26, Puig was placed on the 15-day [disabled list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_list "Disabled list") for the first time in his major league career, due to his nagging left hamstring.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-40) He rejoined the Dodgers roster on June 6.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-41) On August 18, Puig injured his right hamstring, and he was placed on the 15-day disabled list nine days later.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-42) He returned on October 3, appearing in the final two games of the season. He played in a total of 79 regular-season games.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-43) He batted .255/.322/.436, and he had 11 home runs, 38 RBIs, and three stolen bases — all career lows.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44) He batted 0-for-6 in three [NLDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_National_League_Division_Series "2015 National League Division Series") games, starting once.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:5-29)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/2016-10-19_Yasiel_Puig_4.jpg/250px-2016-10-19_Yasiel_Puig_4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2016-10-19_Yasiel_Puig_4.jpg)

Puig in 2016

In the 2016 season, Puig was again hampered by hamstring issues which reduced his playing time and production. He hit .260 with seven home runs in 81 games through the end of July. On August 2, he was optioned to the Triple-A [Oklahoma City Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Dodgers "Oklahoma City Dodgers") when the Dodgers acquired [Josh Reddick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Reddick "Josh Reddick") in a trade to take over the right field position.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-45) ESPN reported that Puig was told by the team on August 1, the day of the trade deadline, not to join the Dodgers on the road since he would either be traded or demoted.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-46) He rejoined the team in September and hit .263/.323/.416 on the season in 104 games with 11 home runs and 45 RBIs.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-47) He batted .211 (4-for-19) with a run scored in 10 postseason games.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44)

#### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2017")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Phillies_vs_Dodgers_2017_40.jpg/250px-Phillies_vs_Dodgers_2017_40.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phillies_vs_Dodgers_2017_40.jpg)

Puig with the Dodgers in 2017

On June 13, 2017, Puig gave the [middle finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_finger "The finger") to fans at [Progressive Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Field "Progressive Field") in Cleveland after hitting a home run.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-48) The next day, he was suspended for a game.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-49) However, his suspension was rescinded following his appeal, and he instead made a charitable donation.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-50) For the season, he batted .263/.346/.487 with 28 home runs (a career high), 74 RBI, and 15 stolen bases.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44) He received the [Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award") for his play in right field.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-51) He had a strong start to the postseason, hitting .455 in the [NLDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_National_League_Division_Series "2017 National League Division Series") and .389 with a home run in the [NLCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_National_League_Championship_Series "2017 National League Championship Series").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44) In the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Series "2017 World Series"), he had only four hits, including two home runs, in 27 at-bats (.148 average) as the Dodgers lost the series in seven games to the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44)

#### 2018

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2018")]

On February 7, 2018, [Wasserman Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasserman_Media_Group "Wasserman Media Group") announced that it had "terminated its professional relationship" with Puig.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-52) He was without representation until April, when he signed with Beverly Hills Sports Council.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-53) On April 28, Puig left a game due to left hip soreness. The injury occurred while he was making a catch against the outfield wall. He was placed on the 10-day disabled list the next day.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-54) On August 11, Puig hit his 100th career home run off [Kyle Freeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Freeland "Kyle Freeland") of the [Colorado Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies "Colorado Rockies"). On August 14, Puig got into an altercation with [Nick Hundley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Hundley "Nick Hundley") at home plate. After fouling off a pitch, Puig threw his bat up and snatched it out of the air in frustration feeling like he had a good pitch to hit. Hundley took exception to Puig's actions and the two had words. Puig then shoved Hundley, causing a bench-clearing brawl. Both Hundley and Puig were ejected.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-55) In 2018, Puig had the lowest fielding percentage among all major league outfielders.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-56) Throughout the season, he struggled against left-handed pitching.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-57)

In Game 7 of the [NLCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_National_League_Championship_Series "2018 National League Championship Series"), Puig hit a three-run home run to extend the Dodger lead to 5–1 against the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers") in a game they would win for their second consecutive [pennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_National_League_pennant_winners "List of National League pennant winners"). In Game 4 of the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Series "2018 World Series"), Puig hit a three-run home run off [Eduardo Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(left-handed_pitcher) "Eduardo Rodríguez (left-handed pitcher)") to increase the Dodger lead to 4–0, although the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Boston_Red_Sox_season "2018 Boston Red Sox season") would win the series in five games.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-58)

### Cincinnati Reds (2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Cincinnati Reds (2019)")]

On December 21, 2018, the Dodgers traded Puig to the [Cincinnati Reds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Reds "Cincinnati Reds"), along with [Matt Kemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Kemp "Matt Kemp"), [Alex Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Wood_(baseball) "Alex Wood (baseball)"), [Kyle Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Farmer "Kyle Farmer"), and cash considerations for [Homer Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_Bailey "Homer Bailey"), [Jeter Downs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeter_Downs "Jeter Downs"), and [Josiah Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josiah_Gray "Josiah Gray").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-59)

Puig was involved in bench-clearing brawls in two Reds losses to the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates "Pittsburgh Pirates") in 2019. The first one in the top of the fourth inning of a 7–5 defeat at [PNC Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNC_Park "PNC Park") on April 7, 2019, resulted in an ejection and a two-game suspension for extending hostilities.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-61) The second brawl was just under four months later on July 30 in the top of the ninth of an 11–4 loss at [Great American Ball Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_American_Ball_Park "Great American Ball Park"), minutes after news broke that he was going to be traded to the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-62)

### Cleveland Indians (2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Cleveland Indians (2019)")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Yasiel_Puig_%2848484235297%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Yasiel_Puig_%2848484235297%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yasiel_Puig_(48484235297)_(cropped).jpg)

Puig at [Progressive Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Field "Progressive Field") in 2019

The three-team trade sending Puig to the Indians became official the following day, July 31, 2019. The Indians also acquired [Scott Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Moss "Scott Moss") from Cincinnati and [Franmil Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franmil_Reyes "Franmil Reyes"), [Logan Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Allen_(baseball,_born_1997) "Logan Allen (baseball, born 1997)"), and Victor Nova from the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres"), the Reds acquired [Trevor Bauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Bauer "Trevor Bauer") from Cleveland, and San Diego acquired [Taylor Trammell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Trammell "Taylor Trammell").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-63) On August 1, Puig was suspended for three games due to his role in a brawl during a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates while playing for the Reds. He did not appeal the suspension, which he served starting on August 12.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-64) He batted .297/.377/.423 with 2 home runs in 49 games with Cleveland. He became a free agent after the season.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-br-44)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-65)

On July 17, 2020, Puig tested positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronavirus_disease_2019 "Coronavirus disease 2019"), nixing a deal he was expected to sign with the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-66) After not playing organized baseball in the 2020 season, he played [winter ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_league_baseball "Winter league baseball") with [Toros del Este](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toros_del_Este "Toros del Este") of the [Dominican Professional Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Professional_Baseball_League "Dominican Professional Baseball League").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:0-67)

### El Águila de Veracruz (2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: El Águila de Veracruz (2021)")]

On April 21, 2021, Puig announced via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that he signed with [El Águila de Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_%C3%81guila_de_Veracruz "El Águila de Veracruz") of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League "Mexican Baseball League").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-68) In 62 games with the team, Puig batted .312/.409/.517 with 10 home runs and 43 RBI in 247 plate appearances.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:0-67) He was named as the Defensive Player of the Year following the season.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-69)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

In April 2013, Puig was charged with [reckless driving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reckless_driving "Reckless driving") and [speeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speeding "Speeding") in [Chattanooga, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chattanooga,_Tennessee "Chattanooga, Tennessee"), after allegedly driving 97 miles per hour (156 km/h) in a 50 mph (80 km/h) zone on Amnicola Highway.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-82) The charges were dismissed after he served 12 hours of [community service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_service "Community service").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-cbssports1-83) On December 28, 2013, Puig was again arrested for reckless driving after allegedly driving 110 mph (180 km/h) in a 70 mph (110 km/h) zone, in [Naples, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples,_Florida "Naples, Florida"). He was taken to the [Collier County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collier_County,_Florida "Collier County, Florida") Jail[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-cbssports1-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-84) and released after posting [bail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bail "Bail"). Prosecutors elected to drop the reckless driving charge on January 28, 2014, after concluding that there was insufficient evidence to support it.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-85)

In March 2021, [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") reported that MLB investigators had interviewed a woman who said Puig had sexually assaulted her in a [Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") bathroom during a [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") game in October 2018. Puig has denied the allegations, calling them "false and malicious". The woman did not file a police report but later filed a lawsuit.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-CloudFuture-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-87) In October 2021, Puig announced that he had settled his sexual assault lawsuit and wished to return to MLB in 2022.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-88)

In December 2021, _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ reported that Puig had secretly settled a lawsuit filed by two women who claimed that Puig sexually assaulted them in January 2017. Despite the allegations, Puig had not been put on leave, and the lawsuit was not publicized. As part of the disclosure from the 2020 lawsuit, Puig's attorneys claimed that Puig was insolvent and that his earlier career earnings were nearly exhausted. The latest settlement was for $250,000, with the accuser paying her own attorney's fees, due to fears that Puig had nothing left to offer had the accuser held out for more.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-90)

In November 2022, Puig agreed to plead guilty to lying to federal law enforcement officers regarding bets that he placed with an illegal [sports betting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_betting "Sports betting") operation. He faced up to five years in prison.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-92) Later that month, he changed his plea to not guilty.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-f692-93) In 2025, a federal appeals court agreed with a trial court ruling that Puig's plea deal had not been accepted by a court. He still faced a jury trial regarding the illegal bets, from which he allegedly incurred $282,900 in gambling debts.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-94)

On February 6, 2026, Puig was found guilty of two federal charges: [making false statements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_false_statements "Making false statements") to investigators and [obstructing justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstruction_of_justice_in_the_United_States "Obstruction of justice in the United States").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-95) The guilty findings could result in up to 20 years imprisonment; sentencing was set for May 26, 2026, but was later pushed back to June 30, 2026, following a post-trial acquittal motion from Puig.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-97) On June 26, 2026, Judge [Dolly M. Gee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Gee "Dolly Gee") agreed to a request from Puig to postpone his sentencing from June 30, 2026, to July 28, 2026, to give him more time to report his finances to the court.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-98)

### Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yasiel_Puig&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

[![Image 14: Yasiel Puig, facing away, wearing a black Cleveland uniform with "Wild Horse" written on the back.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Puig_Wild_Horse_%2848663858233%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Puig_Wild_Horse_%2848663858233%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Puig_Wild_Horse_(48663858233)_(cropped).jpg)

Puig wearing a "Wild Horse" jersey in 2019.

Puig created the Wild Horse Children's Foundation in 2016. The foundation's name embraces the nickname [Vin Scully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_Scully "Vin Scully") gave him in 2013.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-99)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-:2-80) According to its website, the foundation aimed to inspire children and families in underserved communities by promoting healthier and better-quality lives through education, sports, community development, and health and wellness programs.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-100)

On April 19, 2018, Puig and the Wild Horse Children's Foundation announced a collaboration with the City of [San Fernando, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando,_California "San Fernando, California") to renovate Pioneer Park and refurbish a dilapidated house on-site that had been boarded up for nearly 10 years.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-101)

At a game in New York in May 2019, Puig met a young fan about to have his 40th surgery, due to [hydrocephalus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocephalus "Hydrocephalus").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-102) The following month, Puig treated the fan and his family to a Reds game in Cincinnati.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-103)

On an off-day in New York between two Indians' series (one with the [Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets") and one with the [Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees")) in August 2019, Puig paid for a helicopter trip to Camp Simcha, an orthodox Jewish day camp for kids with cancer. He spent four hours with the children there and found it difficult to leave. In a tweet afterward, Puig called it "one of the best days of my life", adding, "you are my inspiration".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasiel_Puig#cite_note-104)
